content:
2017年10月19日，時任北京市長陳吉寧出席在北京人民大會堂舉行的中共十九大會議。(Lintao Zhang/Getty Images)
【大紀元2026年11月25日訊】（大紀元記者唐兵綜合報導）11月24日，中共上海市委書記陳吉寧被查。網民猜測，下一個會是誰。
在中共當局通報陳吉寧落馬消息後，獨立評論人李承鵬在X上發帖表示：上海雖然是出接班人的城市，但也是個要命的地方，陳良宇就是從這裡進了秦城。坐上去（當上上海市委書記）的人，要麼上天，要麼落地，沒有第三條路。陳吉寧在上海會見馬英九、馬斯克、摩根大通的戴蒙、美國商務部長雷蒙多、舒默帶的參議員團、英國首相斯塔默。見得多了，名聲就出去了。2024年李顯龍見完他，海外開始猜他接班。2025年美國《外交事務》乾脆把他寫進了接班人名單。在中國，被外國人看好，從來不是福氣。
2024年11月28日，新加坡前總理、時任國務資政李顯龍訪問上海，與陳吉寧會面。李顯龍在訪華行程結束前接受新加坡媒體訪問時，提到希望與中共「下一代領導人」建立新的聯繫。由於相關視頻及媒體畫面同時出現他與陳吉寧的互動畫面，海外媒體開始討論陳吉寧是否可能成為習的下一代接班人。（鏈接）
今年9月，《日經亞洲》文章分析新任上海市長朱忠明「接班」可能性時，也曾提及李顯龍訪問上海、會見陳吉寧之後，發表「我也希望與中國（中共）下一代領導人們建立新的聯繫」的言論。文章說，因為李顯龍會晤陳吉寧之前，剛剛在北京見過習近平，當時外界熱議李顯龍是不是已經得知中共人事布局。
文章說，這場「接班」猜測對陳吉寧而言，恐怕並非好事。只要外界認為他有意取代習近平，即使只是些微的政治野心，都可能招致習近平不滿，斷送政治前途。據知情人士透露，當時陳吉寧及其身邊人士極力阻止相關消息在中國境內擴散，以免升溫成為中共黨內議題。
美國《外交事務》（Foreign Affairs）2025年10月2日曾刊出專家對談，直接將陳吉寧列為可能的潛在接班人選。理由包括：陳是上海市委書記，這個職位具有特殊政治象徵；他是政治局中相對年輕的成員；他的行政履歷包括中央部會、北京及上海；如果習在2032年前後交棒，陳吉寧在年齡上仍有一定可能性。
獨立時評人蔡慎坤在X上發文說，在習近平看來，誰想成為接班人，誰有可能成為接班人，誰就是最危險的人。
美國飛天大學人文科學系教授章天亮對新唐人表示，陳吉寧存在的本身是讓習近平顯得相當的沒面子，「因為陳吉寧英文很好，而且確實是個學霸，而且在工作上也非常的有水平，尤其是外界對他的這種接班的期待，都可能會讓習近平如芒刺在背。習近平如果想在二十一大真正連任的話，凡是比他強的人，我覺得可能都會進入他的瞄準鏡。」
新加坡有意跟中共所謂「第六代領導集體」培養關係，但其接觸的官員接二連三出事。新加坡方面接觸過的潛在人選中，孫政才2017年落馬，胡春華2022年以後被邊緣化，馬興瑞2026年落馬，陳吉寧2026年被查，陳敏爾兩次沒進政治局常委，李幹傑2025年從中組部調任統戰部被認為是仕途受挫，剩下的張國清和袁家軍也可能因為年齡、資歷和弊案等問題，被攔在接班人選之外。
北京市委書記尹力2025年曾赴新加坡訪問，並與新加坡總理有接觸，目前尚未出事。
在陳吉寧落馬後，海外網民熱議：「還有劉建超，在新加坡參加論壇，聯合早報社長直接說『有沒有可能接外長』。」「下一個該輪到誰了？李強了吧。」「新加坡什麼時候國事會見習主席？儘快排上日程！」「本來尹力可能沒事，被新加坡這一會面，要出事了。」
中國問題專家李林一表示，尹力可能會被認為沒野心當接班人，但是腐敗也是肯定的，中共內鬥激化，會不會也動到尹力，目前還需觀察。
獨立評論人杜政認為中共沒有所謂第六代。他5月在台媒《上報》發文指出，近年「妄議中央」的官員越來越多，說明事實上誰也不將習放在眼裡，只是表面奉承。也有許多官員被查出，私下看的是中共眼中的「反動政治書刊」，這是一股新潮流，更多沒被查出的官員只是不動聲色。未來無論誰接管這個政權，都要清除邪惡腐爛的共產黨。在中共，習近平是「最後一代」，之後沒有來者。

title: 陳吉寧落馬 內幕消息紛傳：習殺瘋了
summary: 2023年3月11日，（由左至右）代表黃坤明、胡春華、陳吉寧、張國清、何衛東出席在北京舉行的全國人民代表大會第四次全體會議開幕式。(Lintao Zhang/Getty Images) 【大紀元2026年11月25日訊】（大紀元記者唐兵綜合報導）中共二十一大前高層內鬥激烈。中央政治局委員、中共上海市委書記陳吉寧突然被宣布落馬。陳吉寧被廣泛認為是習近平「清華幫」成員之一。消息令網絡炸鍋，海外社交平台紛傳各種「內幕消息」，爆料指習真是殺瘋了，現在誰都不信，誰都可能是下一個。評論人
content:
2023年3月11日，（由左至右）代表黃坤明、胡春華、陳吉寧、張國清、何衛東出席在北京舉行的全國人民代表大會第四次全體會議開幕式。(Lintao Zhang/Getty Images)
【大紀元2026年11月25日訊】（大紀元記者唐兵綜合報導）中共二十一大前高層內鬥激烈。中央政治局委員、中共上海市委書記陳吉寧突然被宣布落馬。陳吉寧被廣泛認為是習近平「清華幫」成員之一。消息令網絡炸鍋，海外社交平台紛傳各種「內幕消息」，爆料指習真是殺瘋了，現在誰都不信，誰都可能是下一個。評論人士認為，這些傳言難以證實，但可能對應一些問題點。
2026年11月24日晚，新華社通報稱，中共中央政治局委員、上海市委書記陳吉寧「涉嫌嚴重違紀違法」，正接受中央紀委國家監委審查調查。官方未公布具體指控細節。
消息出來後，大陸網民紛紛表示，「大老虎。」「重磅新聞。」「大為震撼。」「大魚！」「不得了。」「這已經不僅僅是虎了。」「什麼情況。」「在北京就有問題了。」「抓不完，根本抓不完。」
前內蒙古官員杜文發帖：「國內凌晨才收到一些略微靠譜點的信息，關於陳吉寧落馬的原因，老杜在此分享四條：1. 涉及清華學弟北京常務副市長夏林茂案；2. 涉及中共黨內元老醞釀最高領導人接班問題；3. 涉及在留學期間被策反，國安針對陳吉寧進行的祕密調查期間發現其與老幹部有串謀大位問題；4. 涉及在上海為李強家族謀取經濟利益問題。」
王鋼蛋：「內部大佬說了陳吉寧的內幕消息：這次落馬不是單純的貪腐，是黨內鬥爭的犧牲品，背後牽扯劉國中、李希、何立峰、蔡奇、黃坤明。上海這邊，朱忠明、李政、陳傑早就向北京告過他，說他獨斷專權，用自己的影響力給央國企負責人違規輸送工程。錢的事更狠：他拿上海人工智能的財政撥款往美國轉移資產。白手套2017年在新加坡、2019年在新西蘭買的別墅都被抄了，涉嫌洗錢，大額資產約6億元。老婆胡清的代理人涉嫌貪腐，在澳門洗錢，用的還是USDT和冷錢包。他還涉魏小東案，上海市副市長陳宇劍也被牽扯進來。子女跑得最快，昨天17:20就從香港飛新西蘭了。」
王鋼蛋另一段「內幕」傳言則稱：「跟一個北京大佬通電話：從陳吉寧來看。老大真是殺瘋了，現在誰都不信。誰都不好使，任何一個在位的都可能是下一個。接下來，可能會有更大的事發生。台灣可能也會提前，因為等不了了。做好準備吧，該備點吃的啥的備點吧。」
網名Moyan說：「北京最新消息：老大親自送陳吉寧四個字『好自為之』。老大去年親自去上海考察AI。陳在上海搞AI大躍進弄了一堆垃圾AI項目拿出來糊弄老大。國家砸了600億進去，一點成果沒產出。今年APEC開完，老大意識到落後太多，直接動怒，把陳直接拿下來了。」
網名Ray Chu Love Hong Kong稱：「跟一個央企大佬通電話：今年夏天就聽說中紀委劉金國那邊盯上陳吉寧了。他跟一個外商打電話，大談什麼『進一步擴大開放』『目光放長遠』『國際化、法治化、市場化』，還暗示外商可以長期布局。結果這通電話被監聽到了，直接踩了老大的紅線。現在北京圈子裡都傳，陳吉寧那套『繼續改革開放』的話，在老大聽來就是『還想跟我對著幹』。」
中國問題專家李林一對大紀元表示，這些各類傳言，可能多半是無法盡信的，但至少可能從某些側面反映了中共權鬥激烈，那些被提及的問題細節，都值得關注。
獨立時評人蔡慎坤在X上發文說，今年7月15日，習近平在陳吉寧的老領導蔡奇陪同下到上海考察，上海市委書記陳吉寧、市長龔正全程陪同。那時候，蔡奇、陳吉寧、龔正恐怕都不知道習近平已經下定決心要拋棄陳吉寧。陳吉寧是陳希推薦的紅人，也是蔡奇在北京市的搭檔，清除低端人口的支持者和執行者。陳吉寧官宣落馬，必然連累到陳希和蔡奇，還有剛剛卸任上海市長的龔正。龔正11月6日轉任全國人大財政經濟委員會副主任委員，龔正妻子劉茶是劉鶴同父異母妹妹。
11月23日，上海市紀委發布「一週紀事」，第一條就是市委書記陳吉寧11月16日出席反腐會議的消息。會上，陳吉寧要求「緊盯案件線索深挖徹查」。24日晚上，新華社報導，陳吉寧涉嫌嚴重違紀違法，正接受中央紀委國家監委審查調查。
從上海官方的活動報導看，陳吉寧被查前最後一次公開露面是在11月19日下午。他當天到中遠海運集團總部調研，並主持了座談會。

# 空军表示，价值 160 亿美元的推进大型合同被错误发布

空军告诉 Breaking Defense，空军正计划授予价值 161 亿美元的先进推进采购合同，但尚未这样做。

作者：[Michael Marrow](https://breakingdefense.com/author/mmarrow/)，发表于 2026 年 11 月 23 日下午 4:43

 分配到犹他州希尔空军基地第 388 战斗机联队第 388 飞机维修中队第 4 飞机维修分队的飞行员共同进行发动机维修。 （美国空军上士扎卡里·鲁弗斯拍摄的照片）

华盛顿——空军发言人告诉《Breaking Defense》，空军正在收回一项错误的授予价值高达 161 亿美元的大型推进工程合同车辆的公告。

11 月 20 日，空军[宣布](https://breakingdefense.com/2026/11/air-force-issues-massive-16b-contract-for-engine-work-to-dozens-of-companies/)已选择 58 家公司作为该军种的先进推进采购合同 (APAC)，该合同将持续到 2041 年。该计划的结构是无限期交付，不定数量合同，意味着空军不一定有义务花掉全部金额。
空军发言人今天证实，发布在五角大楼[每日合同综述](https://www.war.gov/News/Contracts/Contract/Article/4657624/contracts-for-nov-20-2026/)上的该合同是错误发布的，尽管该军种计划最终授予该合同。在向 Breaking Defense 披露信息后，五角大楼随后在 11 月 23 日的合同清单中指出了更正。 [获奖公告](https://www.war.gov/News/Contracts/Contract/Article/4658409/contracts-for-nov-23-2026/)。

美国空军在给《Breaking Defense》的一份声明中表示：“一旦授予，APAC 将作为灵活的企业级合同工具，满足所有生命周期阶段的推进需求，包括科学和技术、研发、测试和评估、生产、维护和现代化。”

空军还确认，到目前为止，计划选择总共 58 家供应商，并且向每家供应商初始支付 1,000 美元，将“支持”参加获奖后的迎新会议。

# $16 billion propulsion mega-contract posted in error, Air Force says

The Air Force is planning to award the $16.1 billion Advanced Propulsion Acquisition Contract, but has not yet done so, the service told Breaking Defense.

By [Michael Marrow](https://breakingdefense.com/author/mmarrow/) on November 23, 2026 4:43 pm

 Airmen assigned to the 388th Aircraft Maintenance Squadron’s 4th Aircraft Maintenance Unit at the 388th Fighter Wing, Hill Air Force Base, Utah, work together to perform engine maintenance. (U.S. Air Force photos by Staff Sgt. Zachary Rufus)

WASHINGTON — The Air Force is walking back an award announcement it made in error for a massive contract vehicle worth up to $16.1 billion for propulsion work, a service spokesperson told Breaking Defense.

On Nov. 20, the Air Force [announced](https://breakingdefense.com/2026/11/air-force-issues-massive-16b-contract-for-engine-work-to-dozens-of-companies/) it had picked 58 companies for the service’s Advanced Propulsion Acquisition Contract (APAC), set to run through 2041. The program is structured as an indefinite delivery, indefinite quantity contract, meaning the Air Force is not necessarily obligated to spend its full amount.

That award, published on the Pentagon’s [daily contract roundup](https://www.war.gov/News/Contracts/Contract/Article/4657624/contracts-for-nov-20-2026/), was posted erroneously, an Air Force spokesperson confirmed today, though the service is planning to eventually award the contract.After the disclosure to Breaking Defense, the Pentagon subsequently noted the correction in the Nov. 23 list of [award announcements](https://www.war.gov/News/Contracts/Contract/Article/4658409/contracts-for-nov-23-2026/).

“Once awarded, APAC will serve as an agile, enterprise-level contracting vehicle for propulsion requirements across all lifecycle phases, including science and technology, research and development, test and evaluation, production, sustainment, and modernization,” the Air Force said in a statement to Breaking Defense.

The Air Force additionally confirmed that a total of 58 vendors so far are planned for selection, and that an initial $1,000 disbursement to each will “support participation” in a post-award orientation conference for the winners.

“Future orders will be competed among the qualified vendor pool as requirements are validated and funded. Specific platforms, scope, funding, contract type, period of performance, and pricing will be established at the individual Delivery Order or Task Order level,” the statement reads.

The vendor pool from the Nov. 20 contract notice features a range of firms, from startups to established engine primes with different areas of propulsion expertise. And the award comes as the Air Force seeks new and more effective ways to power its existing and future platforms, from drone wingmen to large mobility aircraft.

This 36(b) arms sales notification is published to fulfill the requirements of section 155 of Public Law 104-164 dated July 21, 1996. The following is a copy of the attached Transmittal 26-103, Policy Justification, and Sensitivity of Technology.
Dated: November 17, 2026.
Alternate OSD Federal Register Liaison Officer, Department of Defense.
Transmittal No. RSAT 26-103
Notice of Proposed Issuance of Letter of Offer Pursuant to Section 36(b)(1) of the Arms Export Control Act, as amended
(i) Prospective Purchaser: Government of Australia
Major Defense Equipment* $ 0 Other $300 million TOTAL $300 million
(iii) Description and Quantity or Quantities of Articles or Services under Consideration for Purchase:
The following non-MDE items will be included: Theater Mission Planning Center (TMPC) and associated communications systems; TMPC Mission Planning System (MPS); program management; engineering, training, and logistics services to support the development, procurement, and delivery of the MPS; and other related elements of logistics and program support.
(iv) Military Department: Navy (AT-P-FBT)
(v) Prior Related Cases, if any: AT-P-LGJ
(vi) Sales Commission, Fee, etc., Paid, Offered, or Agreed to be Paid: None known at this time
(vii) Sensitivity of Technology Contained in the Defense Article or Defense Services Proposed to be Sold: See Attached Annex
(viii) Date Report Delivered to Congress: October 8, 2026
* as defined in Section 47(6) of the Arms Export Control Act.
Australia—Tomahawk Capability Development
The Government of Australia has requested to buy Theater Mission Planning Center (TMPC) and associated communications systems; TMPC Mission Planning System (MPS); program management; engineering, training, and logistics services to support the development, procurement, and delivery of the MPS; and other related elements of logistics and program support. The estimated total cost is $300 million.
This proposed sale will support the foreign policy and national security objectives of the United States. Australia is one of our most important allies in the Western Pacific. The strategic location of this political and economic power contributes significantly to ensuring peace and economic stability in the Western Pacific. It is vital to the U.S. national interest to assist our ally in developing and maintaining a strong and ready self-defense capability.
This proposed sale will improve Australia's capability to meet current and future threats by enhancing its Tomahawk capability, strengthening its ability to deter regional threats, and improving its homeland defense. Australia will improve its interoperability with U.S. maritime forces and other allied forces as well as its ability to contribute to missions of mutual interest. Australia will have no difficulty absorbing these articles and services into its armed forces.
The proposed sale of this equipment and support will not alter the basic military balance in the region.
The principal contractors will be BAE Systems, located in San Diego, CA; Tapestry Solutions, located in St. Louis, MO; Peraton, located in San Jose, CA; and Leidos, located in Virginia Beach, VA. At this time, the U.S. Government is not aware of any offset agreement proposed in connection with this potential sale. Any offset agreement will be defined in negotiations between the purchaser and the contractor.
Implementation of this proposed sale will not require the assignment of any additional U.S. Government or contractor representatives to Australia.
There will be no adverse impact on U.S. defense readiness as a result of this proposed sale.
Notice of Proposed Issuance of Letter of Offer Pursuant to Section 36(b)(1) of the Arms Export Control Act
1. The Theater Mission Planning Center (TMPC) communications system and Mission Planning Systems (MPS) hardware and software provides the capability to plan, produce, and distribute autonomously created Tomahawk missions to Royal Australian Navy firing units. The Tomahawk mission planning capability contains sensitive technology, hardware, and software that enhances the operational employment of the Tomahawk Land Attack Missile.
2. The highest level of classification of defense articles, components, and services included in this potential sale is TOP SECRET/SENSITIVE COMPARTMENTED INFORMATION.
3. If a technologically advanced adversary were to obtain knowledge of the specific hardware and software elements, the information could be used to develop countermeasures that might reduce system effectiveness or be used in the development of a system with similar or advanced capabilities.
4. A determination has been made that Australia can provide substantially the same degree of protection for the sensitive technology being released as the U.S. Government. This proposed sale is necessary in furtherance of the U.S. foreign policy and national security objectives outlined in the Policy Justification.
5. All defense articles, technical data, and services listed in this transmittal have been authorized for release and export to the Government of Australia.

content:
罗兴亚种族灭绝裁决面临地缘政治考验 - 大西洋理事会
2017 年 8 月 31 日，在孟加拉国特克纳夫，罗兴亚难民在非法越境后被孟加拉国边防卫队扣留，试图躲避暴雨。（路透社/Mohammad Ponir Hossain/档案照片）
康涅狄格州中城——11 月 19 日，国际法院 (ICJ) 裁定缅甸应对罗辛亚社区的种族灭绝负责。这是国际法院首次认定一个国家对种族灭绝负有责任。同日，美国总统特朗普、中国国家主席习近平和俄罗斯总统普京在深圳会晤后发表声明，警告国际刑事法院滥用管辖权。该声明提到了国际刑事法院和“其他类似机构”，其措辞足够广泛，涵盖了联合国主要司法机构国际法院。第二天，缅甸总统发言人在一份声明中提到了三位领导人在国际法庭上的立场，认为国际法院的裁决“不公平”。这表明缅甸执行该判决中规定的措施，特别是对罗兴亚人获得公民身份的保护，可能取决于大国利益所影响的谈判。
这一判决的公民概念表明了真正的利害关系。国际法院承认，剥夺罗兴亚人公民身份是歧视框架的一部分，这与其种族灭绝意图的调查结果有关。尽管如此，它认为给予每个罗辛亚人充分和平等的公民身份“超出了防止另一场种族灭绝的适当保障的范围”。然而，国际法院确实下令采取赔偿措施，包括“确保保护罗兴亚人免受歧视和迫害”。判决书在两处指出，这项措施包括“在获得公民身份方面”和“在获得公民身份方面和在迁徙自由方面保护免受歧视”。
由于法院没有下令缅甸授予罗兴亚人公民身份，罗兴亚人是否真正获得公民身份将取决于在缅甸拥有利益的政府已经参与的政治谈判。从华盛顿对稀土的兴趣到北京的皎漂港口和新德里的加拉丹运输走廊，世界各国政府在就进入其领土和资源问题与缅甸政府进行谈判时，都面临着一个关键选择。他们可以将罗兴亚公民身份纳入政治安排，也可以接受罗兴亚人的持续排斥，以追求自己的战略利益。外部势力应该利用包括贸易在内的影响力，使裁决的实施以及早该实现的公民身份和安全返回之路成为他们支持的任何解决方案的一部分。
国际法院于 2026 年 11 月 19 日在荷兰海牙就指控缅甸对罗兴亚穆斯林少数民族进行种族灭绝的案件作出判决。（路透社/Piroschka van de Wouw）
如果外部势力支持一项让罗兴亚人成为无国籍人的解决方案，那么将他们赶出缅甸的条件将继续存在，而另一次外逃将变得更有可能。法官莱昂纳多·内梅尔·卡尔代拉·布兰特和专案法官纳维·皮莱在联合声明中指出，缅甸确保平等获得公民身份的义务应解读为：

【原文 English Original】
The Rohingya genocide ruling faces a geopolitical test - Atlantic Council
Rohingya refugees try to take shelter from torrential rain as they are held by the Border Guard Bangladesh after illegally crossing the border, in Teknaf, Bangladesh, on August 31, 2017. (REUTERS/Mohammad Ponir Hossain/File Photo)
MIDDLETOWN, Connecticut—On November 19, the International Court of Justice (ICJ) found Myanmar responsible for genocide against the Rohingya community. It is the first time that the ICJ has held a state responsible for committing genocide. On the same day, US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin issued a declaration after their meeting in Shenzhen that warned against jurisdictional abuse by the International Criminal Court (ICC). The declaration named the ICC and “other similar bodies,” language broad enough to cover the ICJ, the UN’s principal judicial organ. The following day, the spokesperson of the Myanmar president referred to the stance of the three leaders on international courts during a statement that deemed the ICJ’s ruling “unfair.” This would suggest that Myanmar’s implementation of the measures ordered in this judgment, especially its protections on access to citizenship for the Rohingyas, could depend on negotiations shaped by the interests of great powers.
This judgment’s notion of citizenship shows what is really at stake. The ICJ recognized that the denial of citizenship to the Rohingya people was part of a framework of discrimination, which was relevant to its findings on genocidal intent. Nevertheless, it considered granting full and equal citizenship to every Rohingya as “beyond the scope” of appropriate guarantees against another genocide. However, the ICJ did order measures of restitution, including to “ensure the protection of the Rohingya from discrimination and persecution.” The judgment noted in two places that this measure includes “with respect to access to citizenship” and “protection from discrimination in accessing citizenship and with respect to freedom of movement.”
Because the court stopped short of ordering Myanmar to grant citizenship, whether the Rohingya actually receive it will depend on political negotiations in which governments with their own stakes in Myanmar are already engaged. Governments across the world that are in talks with the Myanmar government when it comes to getting access to its territory and resources, from Washington’s interest in rare earths to Beijing’s port at Kyaukphyu and New Delhi’s Kaladan transport corridor, face a crucial choice. They can integrate Rohingya citizenship into the political arrangement, or they can accept the Rohingya’s continued exclusion in order to pursue their own strategic interests. Outside powers should use their leverage, including trade, to make the ruling’s implementation and a long-overdue path to citizenship and safe return part of any settlement they support.
The ICJ delivers its judgment in the case accusing Myanmar of genocide against the Rohingya Muslim minority, in The Hague, Netherlands, on November 19, 2026. (REUTERS/Piroschka van de Wouw)
If outside powers back a settlement that leaves the Rohingya stateless, the conditions that drove them from Myanmar will remain, and another exodus will become more likely. In their joint declaration, Judge Leonardo Nemer Caldeira Brant and Judge ad hoc Navi Pillay noted that Myanmar’s obligation to ensure equal access to citizenship should be read into the operative part of the judgment. While recognizing that states have sovereign authority to decide citizenship requirements, they stressed that access to citizenship is necessary for protection and non-recurrence.
Given the current political situation in Myanmar, implementation of this judgment will likely require the cooperation of actors beyond Myanmar’s central government, including the Arakan Army, a nonstate armed group that now controls much of Rakhine State and has also been inflicting abuse on the Rohingyas. Myanmar remains legally responsible for carrying out the restitution ordered by the court and for upholding its obligations under the Genocide Convention, which include preventing and punishing genocide. The court found that Myanmar failed to prevent genocide by civilians acting alongside its security forces, so that duty reaches beyond the state’s own agents. An assurance of safe return from Naypyidaw means little to families going back to townships the Arakan Army controls.
Bangladesh, where more than one million Rohingya refugees now live, seems to have already considered its next diplomatic moves. On November 8, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam talked about engaging with both the Myanmar authorities and the Arakan Army. She raised concerns regarding the wide-ranging opposition in Myanmar to the return of the Rohingyas. This suggests that the Arakan Army’s capture of most of Rakhine from the military, on its own, will not clear the path for the refugees’ return. While the ICJ judgment bolsters the case for a durable return, Dhaka’s negotiations with various actors in Myanmar should continue.
India, too, has interests in Myanmar, in part because of its connectivity ambitions. The port in Sittwe and the Kaladan corridor are part of its Act East strategy to connect the landlocked northeastern states to the Bay of Bengal region. Local businesses are already dealing directly with the Arakan Army, which now holds the territory across the border. On October 31, a Times of India report mentioned a trade agreement between the Siaha district unit of the Mizoram Commercial Vehicles Association and the Arakan Army’s political wing. Indian engagement with Myanmar has been under consideration for a while. As a former Indian ambassador to Myanmar put it last year, “The Chinese openly have relations with all sides; can India afford not to have the same?” Therefore, New Delhi’s reaction to the ICJ judgment appears restrained. While it acknowledged the verdict and supported a sustainable return, it did not use the word genocide.
Citizenship disputes also shape India’s bilateral relations with Bangladesh. After the National Register of Citizens (NRC) exercise left out 1.9 million people from a citizenship registry, the United Nations Refugee Agency warned in September 2019 about the risk of indefinite statelessness. At the time, rights groups warned that it could set off a crisis like the one the Rohingya faced in Myanmar in 2017. The broader geopolitical concern for the region is much about how states distinguish their own citizens from populations they regard as foreign, particularly those communities that are deemed to share ethnic, linguistic, or religious characteristics across the border. Bangladesh has a direct stake in the consequences of this kind of citizenship framing by its two neighbors.
For their part, Chinese policymakers are focused on different kinds of issues when it comes to Myanmar. As Crisis Group has noted, Beijing has long cultivated ties with numerous groups in the country, including the Arakan Army. Beijing’s Belt and Road Initiative and Kyaukphyu goals mean that China has an interest in securing a negotiation between armed actors and the Myanmar authorities. Not surprisingly, while Beijing responded to the ICJ judgment with concern regarding judicial overreach, it offered continued support for dialogue. That keeps China positioned as an intermediary without committing it to enforcement, though Beijing is hardly neutral. Crisis Group notes that it threw the military regime a lifeline in 2024. Bangladesh’s challenge is to obtain Chinese backing for repatriation without Beijing treating the Rohingya’s return as something to settle only after its commercial projects are secure.
The role of the United States reflects another set of tensions. While Washington recognized the Myanmar military’s atrocities as genocide in 2022, its current diplomatic priorities appear to have shifted. As Reuters reported earlier this month, a State Department strategy seeks a ceasefire offering a pathway to peace by 2030, through forums on fiscal federalism and territorial demarcation that it links to access to Myanmar’s rare earths. Washington’s reaction to the ICJ verdict laid out concerns for abuses, and at the same time it noted its concern about “politicization” of the court. The question remains as to whether Washington will prioritize citizenship of the Rohingyas or make it a lower priority compared to its commercial opportunities.
Bangladesh has proposed the UN General Assembly as a platform for mobilizing support and building a coalition to press Myanmar and the Arakan Army to carry out the court’s restitution measures, not least since the country now holds the rotating General Assembly presidency. Along its border with Rakhine state, Bangladesh can expand trade as an incentive for further cooperation. Such tools create openings for negotiations. It is crucial that Rohingya representatives and youth participate in such dialogues when it comes to securing full citizenship rights and future repatriations, with the backing of the international community.
Next, the court ruled that Myanmar must report within two years regarding measures it has adopted to provide restitution and, if applicable, compensation. But there is a risk in moving too fast. Negotiations that result in a hurried repatriation that leaves the Rohingya vulnerable could lead to instability, forced exodus, and ultimately additional atrocities. While the ICJ judgment provides Bangladesh and its partners a diplomatic opportunity, international partners must press for a secure Rohingya citizenship status in Myanmar before embarking on future steps.

# 也门军队称胡塞武装正在逼近政府在亚丁的据点

也门军方周二表示，胡塞武装分子正在从约 60 公里（40 英里）外逼近国际公认的政府据点亚丁，并誓言击退任何袭击。一名军方发言人表示，胡塞武装在红海附近推进以及政府军撤退后，防御工作已经做好准备。

 作者：

 这张截取自安萨鲁拉媒体中心 2026 年 11 月 20 日发布的视频片段的屏幕截图显示了也门伊朗支持的胡塞武装所说的沙特空袭的后果。 ©法新社

# Yemen’s army says Houthi fighters closing in on government stronghold of Aden

Yemen's military on Tuesday said that Houthi fighters were closing in on the internationally recognised government's stronghold of Aden from about 60km (40 miles) away and vowed to repel any assault. A military spokesman said defences were prepared following Houthi advances and government pullbacks near the Red Sea.

[Add France 24 to your favorites on Google to see France 24 content appear first in your search results.](https://f24.my/GDen)

Issued on: 24/11/2026 - 17:51

 2 min Reading time

Share

 By:

 This screen grab taken from video footage released by Ansarullah Media Centre on November 20, 2026 shows what Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis say is the aftermath of a Saudi air strike. © AFP

[Yemen](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/yemen/)'s armed forces said Tuesday that [Houthi fighters](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/houthi-rebels/) were ready to attack the internationally recognised government's stronghold of Aden, vowing to head off any potential assault.

"Yes, Houthi forces are about 60 kilometres (40 miles) from the city. We take that seriously, and we are ready for it," said military spokesman Colonel Majid al-Nuzaili during a briefing.

Read more[Yemen: Why the Houthis may besiege Aden rather than storm it](https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20261118-yemen-why-the-houthis-may-besiege-aden-rather-than-storm-it)

"They are now ready to attack. We have made our preparations to defend Aden."

The comments come on the heels of recent advances by the Houthis this month, as the Yemeni government pulled back its forces from areas near the [Red Sea](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/red-sea/) to reinforce troops "where current circumstances require", with securing Aden and nearby provinces taking priority.

On November 15, six Yemeni sources told AFP the Houthis had seized control of the Al-Maqatirah and Al-Madaribah districts and positioned themselves 60 kilometres from the southern city.

"The situation is not where we want it to be. But it's not as dire as reported," Nuzaili insisted.

"Taking Aden is a hypothetical situation. It will not happen," he said. "Our forces and our government will make sure that Aden is not at risk."

On Tuesday, Yemen's leader Rashad al-Alimi– the head of the country's presidential council– struck a defiant tone in the face of the Houthi threat.

"We trust in the ability of the Yemeni people and their armed forces to end the Houthi threat, no matter how the front lines shift," he wrote in a post on X.

Read more[Yemen's Houthis target Riyadh after Saudi coalition's 'special operation'](https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20261120-yemen-s-houthis-target-riyadh-after-saudi-coalition-s-special-operation)

The Houthis have repeatedly struck the city of Aden in recent weeks, including an assault on October 15 that targeted the presidential palace and left four people dead, according to government military sources.

The Iran-backed group previously launched an unsuccessful bid to seize Aden early in the war in 2015.

Yemen's internationally recognised government has been based in Aden since it was driven from the capital [Sanaa](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/sanaa/) by the Houthis in 2014.

Yemen, embroiled in more than a decade of [civil war](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/civil-war/), was sucked into the wider [US-Iran conflict](https://www.france24.com/en/tag/iran-conflict/) in July when a truce between the Houthis and the Saudi-backed government unravelled.

Since then, the fighting has left more than 1,600 people dead and over 300,000 displaced in the country, the poorest on the Arabian Peninsula, according to the latest UN toll.

2032年快讯：中国的齐射未能击败台湾，北京陷入消耗战 - 大西洋理事会
2018 年 4 月 12 日，中国人民解放军 (PLA) 海军的军舰和战斗机参加在南海举行的军事展示。（路透社/斯金格，来自Reuters Connect）
本文是斯考克罗夫特中心印度-太平洋安全倡议系列“下一场战争的快报”的一部分，其中我们的专家对世界下一场重大冲突可能在最有可能爆发的地区印度-太平洋地区进行了假设。这些消息被称为虚构情报，或“FicInt”，在军队内部使用，让政策制定者为可能的未来做好准备。目的是防止下一场战争爆发。
2032 年，台北——中国第一批导弹和无人机在夜深人静时飞越台湾海峡。有些在咆哮的火焰喷射的推动下划过黑色的天空，而另一些则安静地、几乎看不见地以稳定的速度在黑暗的天空中嗡嗡作响。第一个被拦截导弹击中中国火柱摧毁，其他则在被激光闪光击中时爆炸。有些被小型拦截无人机撞到一边。一些人被自动炮和机枪的火幕击落，曳光弹在黑暗中摸索着目标，越来越多的条纹。
这些联合火力打击——中国对台战争中所宣称的第一次攻击——旨在摧毁台湾的防御，使其军事力量丧失能力，并粉碎台湾人的战斗意志。尽管这些齐射令人恐惧且令人印象深刻，但它们未能实现中国的目标。
一些袭击成功了，坠入港口、机场和军事基地，并向天空喷出滚滚火焰和浓烟。北起台北，南至高雄，台湾一次又一次遭到无情的打击。虽然台湾军事力量的来源是中国的目标，但许多平民也因这次袭击而被屠杀。世界领导人最初等着看台湾是否能够承受住这场冲击，或者是否会像许多分析人士预测的那样迅速崩溃。
但事实证明，台湾的多层防空和导弹防御系统“T-Dome”出乎意料地有效。尽管该公司在 2027 年首次投入运营时（即 2025 年宣布成立两年后）面临性能困难，但其许多自主系统的可靠性迅速成熟。随着中国入侵台湾领空和侵略性海上骚扰的行为逐年变得更加频繁和充满敌意，台湾的总统和指挥官们更加放心地相信 T-Dome 允许自主攻击其认定的敌对目标。
尽管中国在发动袭击之前发起了旨在破坏台湾指挥和控制系统的强大网络攻势，但台湾慷慨地使用了 Anthropic 的 Claude Mythos 等前沿人工智能 (AI) 网络安全模型，发现并修补了几乎所有潜在的攻击向量，从而保持了 T-Dome 和其他系统的运行。对人工智能抱有如此大的信心的争议是不可避免的。战时的防御效果则不然。
T-Dome 证明了这些高风险决策的正确性，在第一轮拦截中拦截了 90% 的中国弹药。这为台湾指挥官赢得了宝贵的时间来分散兵力，使中国更难瞄准他们，采取预先计划

Dispatch from 2032: After Chinese salvos fail to defeat Taiwan, Beijing is trapped in a war of attrition - Atlantic Council
Warships and fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) Navy take part in a military display in the South China Sea on April 12, 2018. (REUTERS/Stringer via Reuters Connect)
This article is part of “Dispatches from the Next War,” a series from the Scowcroft Center’s Indo-Pacific Security Initiative in which our experts provide hypothetical accounts of what the world’s next major conflict could look like in the region where it’s most likely to break out: the Indo-Pacific. These dispatches are styled as fictional intelligence, or “FicInt,” which is used within the military to prepare policymakers for possible futures. The aim is to prevent the next war from ever unfolding.
TAIPEI, 2032—China’s first missiles and drones flew across the Taiwan Strait in the dead of night. Some coursed across the black sky propelled by growling jets of flame, while others quietly and near-invisibly hummed through the dark sky at a steady pace. The first were destroyed by interceptor missiles snaking into Chinese columns of fire, others exploded when hit by flashes of laser light. Some were knocked aside by tiny interceptor drones. A few were downed by curtains of autocannon and machine-gun fire, with the growing streaks of tracer bullets groping for targets in the dark.
These joint firepower strikes—the vaunted first attack of China’s war on Taiwan—were meant to smash Taiwan’s defenses, incapacitate its military force, and shatter the Taiwanese will to fight. While these salvoes were terrifying and impressive, they failed to achieve China’s objectives.
Some of the attacks got through, crashing into ports, airfields, and military bases, and sending plumes of flame and smoke into the sky. From Taipei in the north to Kaohsiung in the south, Taiwan was mercilessly hit again and again. While sources of Taiwanese military power were China’s target, many civilians were also slaughtered by the attack. World leaders initially waited to see whether Taiwan could withstand the onslaught or whether it would quickly fold as many analysts had predicted.
But the T-Dome, Taiwan’s multi-layered air- and missile-defense system, proved unexpectedly effective. While it faced performance difficulties when it first became operational in 2027, two years after its announcement in 2025, the reliability of many of its autonomous systems matured rapidly. As China’s incursions into Taiwan’s airspace and aggressive maritime harassment grew more frequent and hostile year after year, Taiwan’s presidents and commanders became more comfortable putting greater faith in the T-Dome’s permission to autonomously engage targets it identified as hostile.
And while China’s strikes were preceded by a robust cyber offensive aimed at disrupting Taiwan’s command-and-control systems, Taiwan’s generous use of frontier artificial intelligence (AI) cybersecurity models like Anthropic’s Claude Mythos had discovered and patched nearly every potential attack vector, keeping the T-Dome and other systems operational. The controversy about placing so much faith in AI was inevitable; the defensive results in wartime were not.
The T-Dome vindicated those high-risk decisions, intercepting 90 percent of Chinese munitions in the first barrage. This bought Taiwan’s commanders precious time to disperse their forces and make it more difficult for China to target them, take up preplanned fighting positions across their nation, and start fighting back.
Further, the survivability and resilience of many Taiwanese bases, stations, and command posts proved to be highly robust. Many were built underground and were well-protected by dozens of meters of earth and rock. Missile after missile and drone after drone slammed into the vicinity of these underground command posts. While some were disrupted, as antennas were toppled and wiring cut, most remained operational.
Notably, Taiwan’s air force was able to maintain aviation command and control from its underground airbase within Toad Mountain, contributing both to air defense and strike missions of its own. Above-ground targets in Taiwan, such as airfields and main supply routes, were initially cratered and some aircraft were destroyed. But Taiwanese engineers repaired airfields, roads, and bases with alacrity. As a result, such hits resulted only in temporary pauses in Taiwan’s operations and did not amount to debilitating knock-out blows.
With most of its forces intact, Taiwan counter-attacked, firing its own munitions at key targets across mainland China. Many of these were intercepted. But due to the superior quality and reliability of Taiwan’s munitions, and China’s years-long strategic emphasis on offensive rather than defensive capabilities, a disproportionate number of Taiwanese munitions hit their marks.
In addition, the United States, Japan, and other nations provided Taiwan with exquisite intelligence and provided non-attributable, non-kinetic cyber and space capabilities that greatly enhanced the hit-rate of Taiwan’s defensive counterstrikes. Consequently, Taiwan devastated targets such as the ports where China’s amphibious forces were assembling, crippling the invasion before it even got underway. Chinese aviation command-and-control nodes and over-the-horizon radars were also hammered, giving Taiwan’s air force greater freedom of maneuver than most analysts had ever predicted.
The effects on Taiwanese morale were immeasurable. As with the US military’s famous Doolittle Raid on Japan after Pearl Harbor, the physical damage Taiwan inflicted on China was less important than the political and psychological results of Taiwan’s demonstrated resilience. Taiwan was not helpless, and the People’s Republic of China was not an invincible juggernaut.
With the quick, decisive campaign China had envisioned to isolate and invade Taiwan thwarted, the joint firepower strikes pressed on. Days dragged into weeks. Taiwan began running dry on interceptors, cannons began to jam, and even lasers began to burn out. Taiwan was forced to absorb more direct hits from Chinese strikes, even as China’s own magazines ran low.
If the war were evaluated today based on targets hit, the assessment would find that China has a commanding lead. But even with Taiwan’s dwindling munitions, the forces still in the fight have proven disproportionately effective. As the United States painfully experienced during Operation Epic Fury in Iran, even a greatly diminished adversary can still hold the advantage if it fights asymmetrically and selectively. While short on missiles, Taiwan has maintained plenty of launchers and conducted carefully sequenced strikes layered with joint operations and allied intelligence support that continue to bloody China’s nose. China’s Eastern Theater Command has still refused to launch an invasion fleet across the strait, as the mere preservation of Taiwan’s stand-in forces held the amphibious force at risk, making the amphibious invasion appear infeasible.
China—and the world—also grossly underestimated Taiwanese resolve. Despite polling that showed Taiwanese willingness to fight as even higher than that of Ukrainians prior to the Russian invasion in 2022, many analysts were skeptical that Taiwan would hold fast under the pressure of a Chinese offensive. Such analysts had focused primarily on the correlation of forces and means between China and Taiwan, weighing their assessments on numeric comparisons of ships, jets, and missiles available to both sides. This, however, failed to account for qualitative differences in Chinese and Taiwanese systems and societies, or for fundamental human elements that have always characterized the conduct of war. While bombing alone was not China’s plan, China had been as yet unable to launch its amphibious invasion because it could not set the necessary conditions. Bombing alone has never produced capitulation, and it has not here in Taipei.
Moreover, China’s narrative warfare and United Front activities, its strategic co-opting of domestic groups, had also penetrated swaths of Taiwanese society and foreign discourse, influencing pre-war public commentary to give a dim view of Taiwanese will and an overinflated view of Chinese prowess. The extreme pro-unification wing of the Kuomintang, the Chinese Nationalist Party in Taiwan, aligned itself with Beijing before the war. A few American commentators had advocated strategic restraint, isolationism, and nativism, while some American politicians echoed these sentiments, leading many to presume Taiwan would surrender at the first blush with its enemy.
But as with the staunch resolve of Ukrainians, it appears the Taiwanese are prepared to fight for years if necessary to preserve the democracy and way of life they built after ending martial law in 1987. Under attack, as they have seen their people killed in the streets, the Taiwanese have bravely rallied, pro-unification extremists have been politically isolated, and public sentiment in favor of taidu, formal Taiwanese independence, has skyrocketed. Civil-defense initiatives and energy-diversification efforts, which had been maturing for years, have also mentally prepared the population and the entire society to be resilient despite the immediate imposition of incredible hardship across the country.
Beijing now faces a dilemma. Backing down could deal a fatal blow to the credibility of the Chinese Communist Party, while pressing on would mean doubling down on sunk costs and putting the government’s dream of national rejuvenation further out of reach. Caught in a trap of its own making, China has looked abroad to Russia and North Korea for other solutions, while the Central Military Commission has begun to consider limited nuclear strikes to turn the tide in China’s favor.
Magazine depth cuts both ways. Taiwan may run low on munitions first in a future conflict, but even Chinese inventories are not limitless. And because China cannot hit everything at once, it will likely have to focus on high-priority targets, yielding maneuver space for Taiwanese forces.
Range rings also cut both ways. Taiwan falls within the range of most Chinese strike capabilities. China, too, is within range of many of Taiwan’s strike capabilities. If Taiwan is attacked by China, Taiwan will strike back at targets in China—not just at munitions or forces entering Taiwanese territory.
The earth is the most reliable and affordable shield. Interceptors are necessary, but they can be expensive and can quickly run dry under constant barrage. While difficult to scale, subterranean fortifications reduce reliance on interceptors and mitigate China’s ability to effectively target Taiwan’s forces.
Regardless of when, why, and how China may start the fight, the result would likely be a protracted war with Taiwan. Beijing may intend—and pundits may predict—a quick surrender by Taipei, but this is unlikely. There are many “roads to war” and rationales Beijing will claim led to its aggression, and many ways the war might begin, including a quarantine, a blockade, or outright attack. Regardless, China is unlikely to win rapidly or easily, almost inevitably leading to a protracted and costly conflict—if Taiwan continues its defense and resilience efforts.
Even successful strikes rarely deliver knockout blows, and an active defense can prove resilient even under sustained strike campaigns. Defenders will disperse to preserve forces and capabilities, and can rapidly repair airfields, ports, and bases.
When nations are attacked, cohesion surges, even among politically divided states. Blood calls for blood, defenders rally to their flag, and the will to fight becomes stronger than ever.
Third parties are not easily intimidated into total non-participation in wars that impact them. When nations can pursue their interests and frustrate their adversaries at low risk, they will.

title: From horsepower to firepower, Japan draws auto suppliers into major arms buildup
zh_title: 从马力到火力，日本吸引汽车供应商大规模军备建设
summary: 日本横手——多年来，日本制造商 Aster 通过为丰田汽车供应零部件赚钱。但随着该国汽车工业在激烈的中国竞争中举步维艰，Aster 在国防技术领域找到了新的利基市场。其电动机为美国军事技术公司 Anduril 制造的无人机提供动力，自去年进入该领域以来，国防业务收入已增长至十分之一。 “无人机是一项更好的业务，”首席执行官本乡武信 (Takenobu Hongo) 在谈到 Aster 对国防承包的支持时说道，长期以来，这个国家的公民一直对国防承包持谨慎态度。
content:
日本横手——多年来，日本制造商 Aster 通过为丰田汽车供应零部件赚钱。但随着该国汽车工业在激烈的中国竞争中举步维艰，Aster 在国防技术领域找到了新的利基市场。其电动机为美国军事技术公司 Anduril 制造的无人机提供动力，自去年进入该领域以来，国防业务收入已增长至十分之一。 “无人机是一项更好的业务，”首席执行官本乡武信(Takenobu Hongo)在谈到Aster对国防承包的拥护时说道，长期以来，这个几十年来和平主义塑造的国家的公民一直对国防承包持谨慎态度。 “目前，对我们来说，汽车电机的利润并不高。”根据对包括政府官员、公司高管和首相高市早苗内阁顾问在内的九人的采访，东京鼓励日本众多汽车供应商加入该国自二战以来最大规模的军事建设，Aster 的战略重点是其举措的一部分。高市政府希望，利用现有的工业供应链将加速日本的安全转型，加强其防御能力，抵御来自核邻国中国、俄罗斯和朝鲜的威胁。重新军备的努力得到了东京主要安全伙伴美国的支持，美国正在敦促盟国增加武装部队支出。
相关日本内阁批准创纪录的国防预算，旨在威慑中国 日本2026财年的国防预算草案比2025年增长9.4%。这一建设也为日本曾经世界领先的汽车工业提供了一条重要的多元化途径。日本汽车制造商协会的数据显示，到 2025 年，日本工厂的汽车产量将比十年前减少近 90 万辆。路透社首次报道了该行业刚刚进军国防部门的详细信息，以及负责监督国防部采购的采购、技术和物流局 (ATLA) 如何为其提供支持。一名机构官员和四名高管表示，该部门一直在评估 Aster 等供应商，将它们与军火公司配对，并提供新的资金来源。高市内阁顾问 Koko Kato 在帮助引导行业转型方面也发挥了作用。她说，如果国防和汽车之间存在协同作用，汽车制造商“应该抓住机会”。加藤告诉路透社，她在二月份监督了一项单独的贸易部计划的修改，旨在帮助汽车供应商多元化进入国防和其他行业。 ATLA 在回答路透社的问题时表示，它是帮助寻求进入国防工业的公司的联络点，并将继续与其他政府部门合作，鼓励新进入者。高市办公室没有回应问题。
制造业强国高市政府承诺在年底前制定新的安全战略，其中包括支持日本二战战败后最初解散的军火工业的路线图。该计划建立在日本作为制造业强国的传统之上。尽管汽车工业最近出现衰退，日本仍然是世界第三大汽车生产国。该行业每年生产超过 800 万辆汽车，并提供十分之一的就业机会，约有 70,000 家公司生产大量零部件。自 2025 年政治争端以来，中国已将日本附近的海军存在“正常化”。

【原文 English Original】
YOKOTE, Japan — For years, Japanese manufacturer Aster made its money supplying parts for Toyota vehicles.  But as the country’s auto industry struggles in the face of fierce Chinese competition, Aster has found a new niche in defense technology. Its electric motors power drones built by U.S. military technology company Anduril, and defense work has grown to a tenth of revenue since it entered the sector last year. “Drones are a much better business,” chief executive Takenobu Hongo said of Aster’s embrace of defense contracting, which has long been viewed warily by citizens of a country shaped by decades of pacifism. “At the moment, for us, automotive motors aren’t very profitable.” Aster’s pivot is part of a move by Tokyo to encourage Japan’s many auto suppliers to join the country’s biggest military buildup since World War II, according to interviews with nine people, including government officials, company executives and an advisor to Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s Cabinet. Takaichi’s government hopes that tapping existing industrial supply chains will speed up Japan’s security transformation as it bolsters its defenses against threats from nuclear-armed neighbors China, Russia and North Korea. The rearmament efforts are backed by Tokyo’s chief security partner, the United States, which is pressing allies to increase spending on armed forces. Related Japan’s Cabinet OKs record defense budget that aims to deter China Japan's draft defense budget for fiscal 2026 is up 9.4% from 2025. The buildup also offers an important diversification avenue to Japan’s once world-leading auto industry. The country’s factories built nearly 900,000 fewer vehicles in 2025 than a decade earlier, according to the Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association.  Reuters is reporting for the first time details of the industry’s nascent push into the defense sector and how it is supported by the Acquisition, Technology & Logistics Agency (ATLA), which oversees defense ministry procurement. The department has been evaluating suppliers like Aster, pairing them with arms firms and offering new funding streams, an agency official and four executives said. An advisor to Takaichi’s Cabinet, Koko Kato, has also played a role in helping steer the industry’s transformation. If there is a synergy between defense and autos, carmakers “should take the opportunity,” she said. Kato told Reuters she oversaw changes in February to a separate trade ministry program aimed at helping auto suppliers diversify into defense and other industries. ATLA said in response to Reuters questions that it serves as a point of contact to help companies seeking to enter the defense industry and that it will continue to work with other government departments to encourage new entrants.  Takaichi’s office did not respond to questions.  Manufacturing powerhouse Takaichi’s government has pledged to lay out a new security strategy by year-end, including a road map for bolstering an arms industry that was initially dismantled after Japan’s World War II defeat.  The plan builds on Japan’s legacy as a manufacturing powerhouse. Despite its auto industry’s recent decline, Japan is still the world’s third-largest vehicle-producing nation. The industry manufactures more than 8 million vehicles a year and supports one in 10 jobs, with some 70,000 companies making an enormous array of components. Related China has ‘normalized’ naval presence near Japan since political spat of 2025 Given its scale, the massive Chinese flotilla that included coast guard vessels alongside navy warships may have had Taiwan’s maritime neighbor Japan in its sights, military experts say. Skills prized in auto manufacturing, such as precision and electronics manufacturing, as well as quality control, are relevant to arms production, said Pontus Haggstrom, a Japan-based adviser to the auto industry and former CEO of Stellantis Japan.  The industry “also knows how to produce complex products reliably and at scale,” he added.  The case for Japan to draw on domestic manufacturing has also grown as American arms makers struggle to replenish arsenals depleted by conflicts in the Middle East and Europe. Tokyo was the destination for about a tenth of U.S. weapon exports in 2021-25, according to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute. “Customers tell us their traditional suppliers don’t have the capacity,” said Hiroko Suzuki, the chief executive of car-engine component maker Kyowa Industrial, which has received a growing number of orders for prototype drone engines. While Kyowa has long made missile-related components, the defense sideline now comprises 10% of annual sales, up from 3% in spring 2025. Some auto suppliers are also eyeing opportunities to sell to U.S. and European military contractors.  ATLA has been holding events in Tokyo to connect Japanese suppliers with potential Western clients. Some 48 Japanese companies from various industries took part in a September event, twice as many as last year, the procurement agency said. Drone rush ATLA, which in October launched a funding program for the development and testing of new military technology, has encouraged some auto suppliers to produce components for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). The agency has said it is willing to provide millions of dollars in support to projects that advance to prototype development. The upcoming national security strategy is expected to outline plans to arm Japan with fleets of attack and interceptor drones of the kind that have reshaped warfare elsewhere. But domestic industrial production is tiny: The country exported just over 1,100 drones last year, compared with the roughly 123,000 UAVs sold to overseas clients by neighboring Taiwan, according to trade figures compiled by Taiwan’s Research Institute for Democracy, Society and Emerging Technology. While fiscal constraints are likely to force Tokyo to rethink some existing orders for missiles and aircraft, such is Japan’s need for UAVs that drone-related spending will likely be ringfenced, according to an official familiar with budget plans.  Toru Tokushige, CEO of Japanese dronemaker Terra Drone, said ATLA officials recently introduced him to Kaaz, a maker of racing car parts that has developed a small gasoline-powered aircraft engine. Tapping auto suppliers could significantly increase Japan’s drone-building capacity, he said. A spokesperson for Kaaz said that it has consulted with ATLA and is actively pursuing the development of engines for military drones.  Ishikawa Energy Research, a drone startup that attended ATLA’s September forum, is also seeking military applications for its aircraft.  The firm’s UAVs are used mainly for agricultural purposes such as crop spraying, founder Mitsuru Ishikawa told Reuters. But the former Honda engineer said his gasoline-powered drones could also transport heavier defense equipment or conduct longer-range military reconnaissance missions than more common battery-powered models. The firm, which is based in the industrial town of Ota, has already tapped into the sprawling local auto supply chain that feeds carmaker Subaru, with more than 50% of the components in its drones coming from auto suppliers. Ishikawa does not think those firms will object to his military ambitions, in part because Subaru, which is better known globally for its sporty cars, already has a major defense arm. The company has built military aircraft, including attack helicopters, for Japan’s Self-Defense Forces for decades.  Subaru expects defense-related demand to grow and intends to capture those business opportunities, a spokesperson said, declining to give specific forecasts.   Overcoming a taboo The auto industry’s shift to defense contracting is for now largely limited to smaller parts makers, according to five officials and analysts. Japan’s big three automakers — Toyota, Honda and Nissan — have shown little appetite for a defense tilt. They still have substantive businesses in China, which has criticized Japan’s arms buildup. They have also long been wary of the reputational risks that come with the defense sector.  “The company’s basic position at this point is that we will not do anything related to defense,” senior Toyota executive Hiroyuki Ueda said at a results briefing earlier this month. Nissan declined to comment on potential defense work, while Honda said in response to questions that it has no specific plans to enter the sector.  That hesitancy also filters down to their closest suppliers. Mitsubishi Electric chief financial officer Kenichiro Fujimoto told Reuters his company was pursuing a new military drone venture and that tapping auto supply chains made sense. However, he added, automakers were quite resistant to their suppliers doing anything outside the industry. “There’s this odd attitude sometimes, like, ‘Don’t do any work other than ours,'” he said. Aster’s Hongo was also wary that some of his company’s roughly 100 staff might object when he gathered them at his factory in the northern Japanese town of Yokote in November 2025 to announce that Anduril wanted to use their motors.  Instead, the 71-year-old executive received a warm reception. “Everyone was more like: ‘Wow, that’s impressive!’” he said of the meeting.  The commercial opportunities in defense, as well as growing public concern about Japan’s security challenges, would lure many more companies, Hongo predicted.  “In Japan now, there are very few people who think this is somebody else’s problem,” he said. Reporting by Tim Kelly, John Geddie, Daniel Leussink and Maki Shiraki

title: The Jet That Always Shadows Air Force One When The President Travels Abroad

content:
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普最近对中国的访问引起了在线航班追踪器的特别关注。这在很大程度上是因为美国空军目前所有三架基于波音 747 的空军一号飞机——两架较旧的 VC-25A 和新的前卡塔尔 VC-25B“桥”喷气式飞机——都支持了这次旅行。另一架军用 747 飞机，即 E-4B 守夜人飞机，通常被称为“世界末日飞机”，也被发现跟踪该组织往返于亚洲。虽然这在网上引起了很多关注，包括来自国防网站的博客文章，但事实是这绝对是标准做法。 E-4B 只是总统离开该国时上演的大型空中物流芭蕾舞剧的另一部分，尽管是一个非常独特和害羞的部分。空军目前拥有四架 E-4B，也称为国家机载作战中心 (NAOC)，全部驻扎在内布拉斯加州的奥法特空军基地。其中三架飞机以 747-200 型号为基础，于 20 世纪 70 年代首次作为 E-4A 高级机载指挥所 (AACP) 投入使用。这些飞机随后在 20 世纪 80 年代达到了 E-4B NAOC 标准，并最终加入了直接改装为该配置的第四架飞机。多年来，这些喷气式飞机不断升级。
除了支持总统旅行外，守夜人飞机还定期在海外旅行期间运送国防部长（现在也称为战争部长）及其工作人员等。E-4B 守夜人喷气式飞机的库存图片。美国军方 11 月 16 日，搭载特朗普及其随行人员的 VC-25 飞机离开华盛顿特区郊外的安德鲁斯空军基地。大约在同一时间，一架 E-4B 被追踪到从奥法特起飞。特朗普首先对菲律宾进行了短暂访问，然后前往中国。飞机观察员有一个难得的机会看到所有三架 VC-25 停在马尼拉尼诺·阿基诺国际机场。美国空军：美国总统随行人员正在经安克雷奇飞往马尼拉的途中。 VC-25B 25-3300 #AF83F3 AF1 VC-25A 92-9000 #ADFDF9 SAM01 VCz25A 82-8000 #ADFDF8 SAM47 @sipjack1776 @toystark6886 @LadyAstroJet pic.twitter.com/jyDtuggNOe — 约翰尼·双子座(@Borrowed7Time) 2026 年 11 月 16 日 守夜人喷气式飞机分别飞往日本冲绳岛的嘉手纳空军基地。 E-4B NAOC 73-1676 在总统马尼拉之行期间停泊在嘉手纳。信用 RODN Kadena。 pic.twitter.com/FiNBpFBsR9 — MeNMyRC (@MeNMyRC1) 2026 年 11 月 17 日 今天早些时候，所有三架 VC-25 载着​​特朗普和美国代表团其他成员离开中国。当三人开始飞越日本本土时，E-4B 从嘉手纳起飞跟随他们。
美国总统返回美国 特朗普总统及其随行人员本周在结束各种会议后正在从中国返回美国的途中： VC-25B Bridge "AF1" 25-33000 #AF83F3 VC-25A "SAM47" 82-8000 #ADFDF8 VC-25A "SAM??" 92-9000 #ADFDF9 E-4B “TRUCK55” 73-1676 #ADFEB3 KC-46A… pic.twitter.com/Yg9wYmgEGI — DefenceGeek (@DefenceGeek) 2026 年 11 月 19 日 正如开头提到的，在特朗普访问期间，E-4B 跟踪 VC-25 并在嘉手纳进行前沿部署先去菲律宾，然后去中国，这并不奇怪。这是美国总统出国旅行的标准操作程序。在特朗普五月份访华期间，飞行追踪器特别发现了类似的飞机队列。 HANK99 又名“末日飞机”(E-4B NAOC) 从内布拉斯加州奥法特空军基地飞往美国

【原文 English Original】
U.S. President Donald Trump’s recent visit to China has drawn particular attention from online flight trackers. This is in no small part due to the fact that all three of the U.S. Air Force’s current Boeing 747-based Air Force One aircraft – the two older VC-25As and the new ex-Qatari VC-25B “Bridge” jet – have supported the trip. Another militarized 747, an E-4B Nightwatch , commonly referred to as a ‘doomsday plane,’ was also spotted shadowing the group to and from Asia. While this drew a lot of attention online, including blog posts from defense-focused sites, the reality is this is absolutely standard practice. The E-4B is just another part, albeit a very unique and shy one, of the massive aerial logistics ballet that occurs whenever the President leaves the country. The Air Force currently has four E-4Bs, also known as National Airborne Operations Centers (NAOC), all based at Offutt Air Force Base in Nebraska. Based on the 747-200 model, three of these planes first entered service in the 1970s as E-4A Advanced Airborne Command Posts (AACP). Those aircraft were subsequently brought up to the E-4B NAOC standard in the 1980s, and were eventually joined by a fourth example converted straight to that configuration. The jets have been continuously upgraded over the years. In addition to supporting presidential travel, the Nightwatch aircraft also regularly transport the Secretary of Defense (now also referred to as the Secretary of War) and their staff during overseas trips, among other roles. A stock picture of an E-4B Nightwatch jet. US Military The VC-25s carrying Trump and the rest of his entourage left Andrews Air Force Base just outside Washington, D.C., on November 16. An E-4B was tracked heading out from Offutt at around the same time. Trump headed first for a brief visit to the Philippines before traveling on to China. Plane spotters had a rare opportunity to see all three VC-25s parked together at Ninoy Aquino International Airport in Manila. USAF: POTUS entourage en route to Manila via Anchorage. VC-25B 25-3300 #AF83F3 AF1 VC-25A 92-9000 #ADFDF9 SAM01 VCz25A 82-8000 #ADFDF8 SAM47 @sipjack1776 @toystark6886 @LadyAstroJet pic.twitter.com/jyDtuggNOe — Johnny Gemini (@Borrowed7Time) November 16, 2026 The Nightwatch jet headed separately to Kadena Air Base on the Japanese island of Okinawa. E-4B NAOC 73-1676 bedding down at Kadena during the presidential trip to Manilla. credit RODN Kadena. pic.twitter.com/FiNBpFBsR9 — MeNMyRC (@MeNMyRC1) November 17, 2026 All three VC-25s left China carrying Trump and the rest of the U.S. delegation earlier today. As the trio began to pass over Japan’s home islands, the E-4B took off from Kadena to follow them. POTUS Returning to the US President Trump and his entourage are en-route back to the US from China after various meetings this week: VC-25B Bridge "AF1" 25-33000 #AF83F3 VC-25A "SAM47" 82-8000 #ADFDF8 VC-25A "SAM??" 92-9000 #ADFDF9 E-4B "TRUCK55" 73-1676 #ADFEB3 KC-46A… pic.twitter.com/Yg9wYmgEGI — DefenceGeek (@DefenceGeek) November 19, 2026 As mentioned at the start, the E-4B shadowing the VC-25s and being forward-deployed in Kadena during Trump’s visit to the Philippines and then China is no surprise. This is standard operating procedure for when the President of the United States travels abroad. Flight trackers notably caught a similar procession of aircraft during Trump’s trip to China back in May. HANK99 aka “The Doomsday Plane” (E-4B NAOC) is airborne from Offutt AFB, Nebraska to shadow POTUS on his trip to China. https://t.co/BBsq1tkC1E pic.twitter.com/Z3zpxBX9zy — Thenewarea51 (@thenewarea51) May 12, 2026 While the E-4Bs are nowhere near as luxurious as the VC-25As or the new VC-25B, they are just as capable of serving as airborne command posts, if not more so in many respects . They are unofficially referred to as ‘doomsday planes’ because they are specifically configured to provide the president and other senior military officials with a flying headquarters they can use for any and all duties, including directing nuclear strikes during the most serious crises. They are hardened against electromagnetic pulses caused by nuclear detonations and have the ability to stay airborne for days. Their very existence, at least one being on alert at all times to support the National Command Authority , is a critical component that underpins America’s nuclear deterrent. Even if an adversary destroys much of the country, an E-4 can remain airborne to order the counter-attack. With all this in mind, the E-4B fleet is key to so-called continuity of government plans , which are in place to make sure key elements of the federal government remain functional following an attack or a similarly serious contingency. As a prime example, President George W. Bush rode on one of the VC-25A Air Force One aircraft in the immediate wake of the 9/11 terrorist attacks, but there were discussions about transferring him to a Nightwatch jet . Bush ultimately decided against making the change, but an E-4B was still scrambled and orbited over Washington, D.C., for a time. This is hardly the only time a president has made use of an E-4B, or one of its predecessors, as well as command ships, as TWZ has examined in the past . September 11th, 2001 – Boeing E-4B NAOC callsign ADDIS77 scrambled from Andrews AFB. While ATC was calling them “VENUS” which is a typical callsign used at Andrews, you can hear the urgency of the pilot wanting to get airborne. The E-4 orbited over Washington DC for a while… pic.twitter.com/K61yeFY3kZ — Thenewarea51 (@thenewarea51) September 11, 2021 The aircraft got airborne assuming for safety reasons (safer in air than on the ground) and if needed would have flown to pickup the President or next in the line of succession (Continuity of government). — Thenewarea51 (@thenewarea51) September 11, 2021 Within this broader context, E-4Bs have been a key feature of overseas presidential travel for decades now, although they are the least visible of the presidential aerial armada. This massive airlift and logistics effort includes bringing in multiple examples of the presidential motorcade , Marine One helicopters , and various force protection assets . This involves many sorties by C-17 and C-5 cargo aircraft that cover many thousands of miles each. The videos below from Trump’s visit this week to the Philippines give a sense of just one portion of these options, albeit the most visible one, the vertical airlift component. US President Trump landing at Luneta. Impressive to see the extent of securing the safety of the most important human being on the planet. pic.twitter.com/gIXewN6Yz3 — Emil (@13thFool) November 18, 2026 Beyond its strategic command and control mission, having an E-4B positioned in the region the president is visiting during overseas trips offers a critical option for refuge and escape, as well as an additional backup aircraft to Air Force One, should any emergencies arise. The exact parameters for where the Nightwatch aircraft go are unknown, but would be based on what suitable airports are available and what potential threats and contingencies could arise. They are never seen at the same locations as Air Force One and are always separated by a distance of dozens of miles, at least, in friendly countries — close enough to be accessed by Marine One in an emergency — or generally in a region for more sensitive locales where such close proximity basing isn’t an option. It moves in shadow of AF1 everywhere it goes overseas, usually lands at another airport nearby. This is standard procedure going back decades. We see it every single overseas trip. Beyond it's strategic and COG function it acts as a refuge/escape if something really bad happens… https://t.co/nPhxPJOKMk — Tyler Rogoway (@Aviation_Intel) November 19, 2026 E-4Bs do not need to be airborne to act as command and control platforms and secure communications relay nodes, either. This further feeds into their continuity of government role. These are capabilities that can also be made available, if required, to assist the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) during major natural disasters or to help serve as command posts and communications nodes in other emergencies. The changing character of the Air Force One fleet could put new emphasis on the E-4Bs, as well as the replacement E-4C Survivable Airborne Operations Center (SAOC) jets the Air Force is now in the process of acquiring. Trump’s trip back from China has notably underscored a significant difference between the VC-25As and the new VC-25B Bridge aircraft, which is that the latter lacks aerial refueling capability. Two fully-outfitted VC-25Bs that Boeing is still in the process of converting for the Air Force will also not be capable of refueling in flight. The E-4Bs can refuel in flight, and the E-4Cs will be able to do so, as well. Coming back from China heading to DC, the new VC-25B Bridge Air Force One does not need to refuel in Alaska but the old VC-25As do. Tracking via @ADSBex pic.twitter.com/zhcdCaIRyy — Thenewarea51 (@thenewarea51) November 19, 2026 TWZ has previously explored the Air Force’s decision to axe the aerial refueling requirement for the VC-25B in detail. The ostensible logic is that the VC-25Bs are based on newer 747-8i aircraft with more capable and fuel-efficient engines than the aging 747-200-based VC-25As. The new aircraft are, as a result, capable of longer unrefueled flights, though maximum range requirements were also watered down . At the same time, in-flight refueling allows the VC-25As ( as well as the E-4Bs ) to remain aloft for days at a time. This, in turn, could be critical in a major crisis where access to secure airfields might be limited, if not completely unavailable, for a prolonged period of time. An E-4B links up with a KC-135 aerial refueling tanker. USAF The  VC-25B Bridge jet has prompted a whole new array of operational security questions, which TWZ was calling attention to even before the decision was formally made to outfit it for presidential use. The circumstances of Trump’s return from the NATO summit in Turkey in July had prompted a further flurry of reports about whether the modified, Qatari-gifted jet lacked sufficient defensive features and other capabilities in line with the existing VC-25As. The President had flown to Turkey on the Bridge jet, but was reportedly covertly moved between other aircraft on the way back. This was said to have been done as a security precaution amid then-escalating fighting with Iran . A stock picture of the VC-25B Bridge aircraft seen at the time of its official unveiling. USAF President Trump subsequently downplayed the series of events, but said that the Bridge aircraft would be sent to have its capabilities “maxed out.” The White House confirmed that the jet would receive “additional upgrades and enhancements,” but did not elaborate. It is unclear how the aircraft’s configuration has changed in the ensuing months. It is worth noting here that the upgrades in question would have to be limited to defensive systems. The Bridge aircraft could also have entered service without certain communications and networking capabilities found on the VC-25As. Another way to mitigate any such limitations could be to have a VC-25A or an E-4B operating closely enough to establish a line-of-sight data connection relatively quickly so it can leverage the better-equipped aircraft’s communications systems if needed. As an aside, Trump arrived in China aboard the Bridge aircraft and was seen boarding it to head back to the United States. Reporters onboard had their phones taken away during the return flight for still unexplained security reasons. Fox News has reported that the president is aiming to set a record for the longest continuous flight for an Air Force One aircraft. At the time of writing, its unclear whether the president has touched back down anywhere publicly since leaving Shenzhen. Air Force One is about to take off. Press has had their phones confiscated for security reasons. pic.twitter.com/2UkCDekUma — Andrew Leyden (@PenguinSix) November 19, 2026 NOW: Air Force One is setting a new endurance record on the way home from China. In an exclusive chat with @aishahhasnie , President Trump says his trip back to Washington will be the longest continuous flight in Air Force One history. President Trump says he will discuss the… pic.twitter.com/xn25uSkzYZ — Fox News (@FoxNews) November 19, 2026 Where the E-4B is now is also unclear, but it was last tracked continuing along a path shadowing behind Air Force One, where one would expect to see it. Contact the author: joe@twz.com The post The Jet That Always Shadows Air Force One When The President Travels Abroad appeared first on TWZ .

title: Launch Preview: Russian, Chinese, and SpaceX rockets to launch space station missions
zh_title: 发射预览：俄罗斯、中国和 SpaceX 火箭将发射空间站任务
summary: 十枚火箭将于下周发射，其中三枚将访问近地轨道上的两个不同空间站。进步号 MS-36 和 CRS NG-25 预计将向国际空间站运送物资，而神舟二十四号计划将下一批宇航员送入中国天宫空间站，其中包括第一位国际访客。除了空间站飞行之外，猎鹰 9 号还将从范登堡发射两次 USSF 任务，而中国也将向轨道发射四联有效载荷。最后，Electron 将发射一颗合成孔径雷达卫星。联盟号2.1b
content:
十枚火箭将于下周发射，其中三枚将访问近地轨道上的两个不同空间站。进步号 MS-36 和 CRS NG-25 预计将向国际空间站运送物资，而神舟二十四号计划将下一批宇航员送入中国天宫空间站，其中包括第一位国际访客。除了空间站飞行之外，猎鹰 9 号还将从范登堡发射两次 USSF 任务，而中国也将向轨道发射四联有效载荷。最后，Electron 将发射一颗合成孔径雷达卫星。联盟号 2.1b |进步 MS-36 11 月 24 日星期二，俄罗斯向国际空间站 (ISS) 发射了进步 MS-36。 Progress MS-36 于世界标准时间 10:13 从哈萨克斯坦拜科努尔航天发射场的 Site 31/6 升空。 Progress MS-36，也被 NASA 称为 Progress 97P，是对国际空间站的补给任务。 Progress 是一艘源自联盟号的航天器，能够携带约 2.5 吨的货物到国际空间站。 Progress MS-36 是 Progress 的第 189 次飞行，于 1978 年首次飞行并与礼炮 6 号空间站对接。 Progress MS-32 从拜科努尔航天发射场升空。 （图片来源：NASA+）联盟 2.1b 是一款三级煤油和液氧运载火箭，源自 R-7 洲际弹道导弹。联盟号 2.1b 可以向近地轨道 (LEO) 输送高达 8,700 公斤的重量。可以配备可选的第四级 Fregat 或 Volga，用于最终轨道调整。
周二的飞行将是联盟号 2.1b 2026 年的第 10 次飞行，也是整体的第 109 次飞行。 阿丽亚娜 64 |亚马逊狮子座 (LE-04) 在周二的三次发射中的第二次，阿丽亚娜 64 火箭向近地轨道发射了另一批 36 颗亚马逊狮子座卫星。发射窗口于世界标准时间 10:45 开始，并延长至世界标准时间 11:14，阿丽亚娜 6 号在该窗口结束时发射。这次发射是阿丽亚娜 6 号计划进行的 18 次狮子座发射中的第四次。阿丽亚娜 6 是由阿丽亚娜集团为欧洲航天局开发的两级液氢和液氧动力火箭。阿丽亚娜 6 可以配备两个或四个固体火箭助推器来增加升空推力，LE-04 则配备四个。周二的发射是 2026 年阿丽亚娜 6 号的第五次发射任务，也是总共的第十次飞行。阿丽亚娜 64 在 LE-01 任务期间上升（图片来源：ESA/M. Pédoussau） Falcon 9 | USSF-266 在周二的第三次发射中，猎鹰 9 号为美国太空军 (USSF) 发射了一个机密有效载荷。 USSF-266 原定于 11 月 23 日星期一从加利福尼亚州范登堡太空部队基地 (VSFB) 于 11 月 24 日发射升空。 USSF-266 的发射窗口于太平洋标准时间上午 7:55（世界标准时间 15:55）开始，并延长至太平洋标准时间上午 11:55（世界标准时间 19:55），猎鹰 9 号于太平洋标准时间上午 11:08（世界标准时间 19:08）发射。根据空投区，USSF-266 很可能是 USSF 天基机载移动目标指示器计划 (SB-AMTI) 的一部分。 SB-AMTI 是在 Starshield 卫星总线的基础上构建的，而 Starshield 卫星总线本身又源自 Starlink 卫星总线。
助推器 B1081 进行了第 29 次飞行，之前曾飞行过 Crew 7、CRS-29、PACE、Transporter 10 和 13、EarthCARE、NROL-186 和 -48、TRACERS & Others、CSG-3、USSF-153 和 USSF-481。这款特殊助推器是从 SpaceX 目前所有活跃的 Falcon 9 发射台上进行过飞行的少数助推器之一。 B1081 在发射后大约八分钟降落在 SpaceX 的无人机“当然我仍然爱你”在太平洋上。长征2F/G |神舟二十四号周三，中国向天宫空间站发射了下一次载人飞行任务。她

【原文 English Original】
Ten rockets are set to launch over the next week, with three visiting two different space stations in low-Earth orbit. Progress MS-36 and CRS NG-25 are expected to deliver supplies to the International Space Station, while Shenzhou 24 is scheduled to launch the next crew to the Chinese Tiangong Space Station, including its first international visitor. Outside of space station flights, Falcon 9 is set to launch a pair of USSF missions from Vandenberg, and China is set to launch a quadruple-header of payloads to orbit. Lastly, Electron will launch a synthetic aperture radar satellite. Soyuz 2.1b | Progress MS-36 On Tuesday, Nov. 24, Russia launched the Progress MS-36 to the International Space Station (ISS). Progress MS-36 lifted off at 10:13 UTC from Site 31/6 at the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan. Progress MS-36, also called Progress 97P by NASA, is a resupply mission to the ISS. Progress is a Soyuz-derived spacecraft capable of carrying around 2.5 tonnes of cargo to the Station. Progress MS-36 served as the 189th flight of Progress, which first flew in 1978 and docked with the Salyut 6 space station. Progress MS-32 lifts off from Baikonur Cosmodrome. (Credit: NASA+) Soyuz 2.1b is a three-stage kerosene-and-liquid-oxygen launch vehicle derived from the R-7 intercontinental ballistic missile. Soyuz 2.1b can deliver up to 8,700 kg to low-Earth orbit (LEO). An optional fourth stage, Fregat or Volga, can be equipped for final orbital adjustments. Tuesday’s flight will be the 10th Soyuz 2.1b flight in 2026 and the 109th overall. Ariane 64 | Amazon Leo (LE-04) The second of three launches on Tuesday saw an Ariane 64 rocket deliver another batch of 36 Amazon Leo satellites to LEO. The launch window opened at 10:45 UTC and extended until 11:14 UTC, with Ariane 6 launching at the end of the window. This launch was the fourth of 18 Leo launches scheduled on Ariane 6. Ariane 6 is a two-stage, liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen-powered rocket developed by ArianeGroup for the European Space Agency. Ariane 6 can be equipped with either two or four solid rocket boosters to augment liftoff thrust, with LE-04 flying with four. Tuesday’s launch was the fifth Ariane 6 mission of 2026, and the 10th flight overall. Ariane 64 ascents during the LE-01 mission (Credit: ESA/M. Pédoussau) Falcon 9 | USSF-266 The third launch on Tuesday saw Falcon 9 launch a classified payload for the United States Space Force (USSF). Originally scheduled for Monday, Nov. 23, USSF-266 launched on Nov. 24 from Vandenberg Space Force Base (VSFB) in California. The launch window for USSF-266 opened at 7:55 AM PST (15:55 UTC) and extended until 11:55 AM PST (19:55 UTC), with Falcon 9 launching at 11:08 AM PST (19:08 UTC). Based on drop zones, USSF-266 is most likely part of the USSF’s Space-Based Airborne Moving Target Indicator Program (SB-AMTI). SB-AMTI is built off of the Starshield satellite bus, which itself is derived from the Starlink satellite bus. Booster B1081 flew its 29th flight after previously flying Crew 7, CRS-29, PACE, Transporter 10 and 13, EarthCARE, NROL-186 and -48, TRACERS & Others, CSG-3, USSF-153, and USSF-481. This particular booster is one of a few boosters to have flown from all of SpaceX’s currently active Falcon 9 pads. B1081 landed on SpaceX’s droneship Of Course I Still Love You in the Pacific approximately eight minutes after launch. Chang Zheng 2F/G | Shenzhou 24 On Wednesday, China launched its next crewed mission to its Tiangong Space Station. Shenzhou 24 lifted off from Site 91 at the Jiquan Satellite Launch Complex (JSLC). The launch is currently set for 10 minutes into a 40-minute-long window at 00:18 UTC. The crew was launched aboard a Chang Zheng 2F/G (CZ-2F/G) rocket, which has carried every Chinese crewed mission to date. The three-person crew flew to Tiangong aboard the Shenzhou spacecraft, which borrows many characteristics and designs from Russia’s crewed Soyuz vehicle. Chang Zheng 2F/G with Shenzhou 24 leaves the assembly building. (Credit: CCTV) Shenzhou 24 features a crew of three astronauts, with two Chinese taikonauts, Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi, and one Pakistani astronaut, Muhammad Zeeshan Ali. Shenzhou 24 will be Ali’s first spaceflight, and he will spend a short duration aboard Tiangong. This flight marks the first time a non-Chinese astronaut has ever visited Tiangong, which has been in orbit since 2021. The CZ-2F/G is a two-stage, hypergolic rocket equipped with four side boosters that stand 58 m tall. The vehicle is fueled by dinitrogen tetroxide and unsymmetrical dimethyl hydrazine (UDMH), both of which are highly carcinogenic. Shenzhou 24 will be the 18th crewed Chinese flight and the 24th overall in the Shenzhou program. Chang Zheng 2D | Unknown Payload The first of two launches on Thursday features a Chang Zheng 2D (CZ-2D) that will deliver an unknown payload to orbit. This mission is set to liftoff at 09:35 UTC, five minutes into a 22-minute window, from Launch Complex 3 (LC-3) at the Xichang Satellite Launch Center. CZ-2D is a two-stage launch vehicle, with an optional third stage, standing 41 m tall. The rocket is powered by hypergolic fuels and is capable of lofting 3,500 kg to LEO. Thursday’s flight will be the eighth mission of 2026 for CZ-2D, and the 109th overall. Electron | Night Owls Never Sleep Flying from the Mahia Peninsula in New Zealand on Friday, Nov 27, Rocket Lab’s Electron will launch a synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite to LEO for Synspective. The mission, named “Night Owls Never Sleep,” is scheduled to liftoff at 00:05 UTC. SAR is used to image the surface of the Earth and can penetrate through cloud layers. Launch 101 coming right up. We're preparing to launch our 101st Electron next week to deploy another StriX Earth-imaging spacecraft for @synspective . The "Night Owls Never Sleep" launch window opens: 1:00 pm NZDT, Nov 27 00:00 UTC, Nov 27 9:00 am JST, Nov 27 7:00 pm… pic.twitter.com/pfblD6s70R — Rocket Lab (@RocketLab) November 20, 2026 Electron is a two-stage, small-lift vehicle capable of delivering up to 300 kg to LEO. The vehicle is fueled by liquid kerosene and liquid oxygen, which powers nine Rutherford engines on the first stage and a single vacuum-optimized Rutherford on the second stage. This mission will serve as Electron’s 22nd mission of 2026 and 101st overall. Chang Zheng 6A | Unknown Payload On Friday, China is set to launch a Chang Zheng 6A (CZ-6A) from the Taiyuan Satellite Launch Center, carrying an unknown payload into orbit. The launch window opens at 12:53 UTC and extends until 13:15 UTC. Currently, liftoff is scheduled for seven minutes into the window at 13:00 UTC. CZ-6A is a two-stage, liquid kerosene-and-liquid-oxygen rocket capable of delivering up to 8,000 kg to LEO. CZ-6A is additionally powered by four solid rocket boosters, which augment first-stage thrust. The vehicle stands 50 m tall with a normal fairing or 52 m tall with an extended fairing. This flight will serve as the 10th CZ-6A mission of 2026 and 29th overall. Chang Zheng 6C | Unknown Payload The last launch of the week from China features a Chang Zheng 6C (CZ-6C) also launching from Taiyuan, delivering an unknown payload to LEO. The launch window opens at 03:46 UTC and extends until 04:15 UTC, with liftoff scheduled for 03:50 UTC, four minutes into the window. CZ-6C is a two-stage, liquid kerosene- and liquid oxygen-powered rocket capable of delivering 4,500 kg to LEO. CZ-6C stands 43 m tall and is considered a single-stick variant of CZ-6A, flying without the solid rocket boosters. Sunday’s launch will be CZ-6C’s second of 2026, and third overall. Falcon 9 | USSF-380 Falcon 9 is set to fly again from VSFB on Sunday, delivering USSF-380 to LEO for the USSF. The launch window opens at 8:39 PM PST on Nov. 28 (04:39 UTC on Nov. 29) and extends until 2:39 AM PST (08:39 UTC, both on Nov. 29). USSF-380 is a classified mission for the USSF but is believed to be part of its Space-Based Sensing and Targeting (SBST) portfolio. SBST is built off of the Starshield satellite bus. The exact number of satellites being launched is unknown but is believed to be similar to that of a typical Starlink mission, based on Falcon 9’s drop zones. Booster B1082 will support this mission on its 27th flight. B1082 has previously supported USSF-62 (WSF-M 1), OneWeb #20, NROL-145, Transporter 18, and 22 Starlink missions. Following stage separation, B1082 will land aboard SpaceX’s droneship Of Course I Still Love You approximately eight minutes after launch. Falcon 9 | CRS NG-25 The final launch of the week will see a Falcon 9 deliver the CRS NG-25 cargo resupply mission to the ISS. CRS NG-25 will launch from Space Launch Complex 40 (SLC-40) at the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station (CCSFS) in Florida, with the instantaneous launch window opening on Sunday, Nov 29, at 10:50 AM EST (15:50 UTC). Cygnus XL approaches the ISS for berthing. (Credit: NASA) CRS NG-25 will be the fifth of six planned Cygnus flights aboard Falcon 9, as Northrop Grumman and Firefly Aerospace work to bring their upcoming Antares 330 rocket online in the near future. Additionally, CRS NG-25 will be the third flight of Cygnus XL, which can carry 5,000 kg of cargo to the Station. CRS NG-25’s Cygnus XL is named “ SS James ‘Jim’ Lovell ” after the Apollo 8 and Apollo 13 astronaut who passed away in August 2025. Supporting CRS NG-25 will be booster B1096 on its ninth flight. B1096 has previously supported the Starlink Group 6-87, KF-01, NROL-77, NROL-95, GPS III SV09, CRS-34, CRS-35, and IMAP & Others missions. The booster will return to CCSFS to land at Landing Zone 40 (LZ-40), which is located directly adjacent to SLC-40. Sunday’s recovery attempt will be Falcon 9’s 700th attempted recovery, of which 682 have been successful. CRS NG-25 will serve as the 125th Falcon 9 mission and the 281st orbital launch attempt worldwide in 2026. (Lead Image: Falcon 9 launches from Florida. Credit: Julia Bergeron for NSF) The post Launch Preview: Russian, Chinese, and SpaceX rockets to launch space station missions appeared first on NASASpaceFlight.com .
