Malaysia talks with US on AI chip curbs, tightens controls | The Straits Times
Malaysia talks with US on AI chip curbs, tightens controls
Sign up now: Get insights on the biggest stories in Malaysia
According to CIMB Bank, Malaysia stands to lose the most in South-east Asia due to the latest US chip restrictions.
Published Nov 25, 2026, 04:23 PM
Updated Nov 25, 2026, 04:23 PM
Malaysia is talking with the US on AI chip curbs and says it will comply with new rules while tightening controls after Nvidia chip smuggling concerns.
The US now requires licences for advanced AI chip purchases in Malaysia and nearby countries, to block China from offshore computing power.
Malaysia says its data centre and cloud investment remains strong, but CIMB warns the curbs could trim GDP growth by 0.19 percentage point in 2027.
KUALA LUMPUR – Malaysia’s second finance minister Amir Hamzah Azizan downplayed the impact of new US curbs on the use of high-end chip technology in South-east Asia, saying the country is ensuring compliance with rules and that its technology is widely used beyond artificial intelligence.
Malaysia’s Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry is holding discussions with the US on the issue, and expects both sides will find common ground, Amir said in an interview with Bloomberg TV’s Haslinda Amin on Nov 25.
“We will comply” with whatever rules are set by the relevant country.
Concerns that high-end Nvidia Corp chips are being smuggled to China through South-east Asia, the US has blacklisted several entities in the region from access to the technology, including three it said were Malaysian.
While Kuala Lumpur has since said only two of the three are Malaysian, it has pledged to tell data centre operators not to host, lease space to or provide services to the blacklisted firms.
Amir said Malaysia had not approved the shipments being questioned and that the South-east Asian nation is taking steps to prevent similar incidents.
“This is in relation to the Nvidia issue,” he said. “Effectively we’re just tightening up controls.”
Data centre operators in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia will need a US government license to purchase advanced AI chips from Nvidia and other American manufacturers, according to an interim rule released by the Commerce Department last week.
The measure seeks to restrict China and other US adversaries from accessing offshore computing power that uses American-designed processors.
Amir said there are many reasons companies seek compute.
“Hyperscalers in Malaysia are generally western-dominated, and they use it predominantly for their own internal capacity,” he said. “Data centre buildouts are not just for AI but they are also for cloud services and all these elements.”
According to CIMB Bank Bhd, Malaysia stands to lose the most in South-east Asia due to the latest US chip restrictions.
GDP growth could be 0.19 percentage point lower in 2027 under CIMB’s worst-case scenario of a six-month disruption to data centre operations and a postponement of 25% of ongoing construction capacity.
“Malaysia’s lead in ASEAN data centre buildout is a double-edge sword. Its dominance in live AI capacity, alongside substantial construction and planned pipeline across all workloads, leaves it exposed to the direct and grey-area regulatory risks,” CIMB said in the Nov 19 report.
Malaysia has said it approved RM350.4 billion (S$109.84 billion) of investments in the first nine months of 2026, up 21% from a year earlier, with data centre and cloud projects accounting for more than a third of the total at RM123.5 billion.
Record high exports from sustained demand for AI-related products helped Malaysia’s economy expand 5.5% in the third quarter, putting it on track to beat the government’s revised forecast of 4.8% to 5.3% growth in 2026.
Amir, who declined to address whether he will seek reappointment when his three-year Senate term expires on Dec 11, said demand will remain solid.
“I think the the reality is compute demand will continue to move on,” Amir said. BLOOMBERG

Huang was promoted during a ceremony at the Presidential Office presided over by President Lai Ching-te (賴清德).
Huang previously served as public affairs director at Army Command Headquarters, where she was responsible for psychological warfare and media relations.

content:
台湾漫画大受欢迎，习近平的笑话不断出现海峡时报
台湾漫画大受欢迎，习近平笑话不断出现
立即注册：深入了解亚洲的快速发展
台湾喜剧演员黄一豪在台北二三喜剧俱乐部表演。
发表于 2026 年 11 月 25 日 02:00
更新于 2026 年 11 月 25 日 02:05
尽管威胁要求他提供安全细节，但台湾喜剧演员黄义豪一直以中国领导人习近平为笑柄。
检察官称，五人密谋用汽车“打断他的胳膊和腿”。九月份黄被击中并受轻伤后，嫌疑人被起诉。
台北称之为中国的“跨国镇压”，称其威胁言论自由。北京否认参与其中，并表示台湾正在利用此案谋取政治利益。
台北 — — 在民主的台湾，即使是一位单口相声演员，在讲笑话时也会有保安人员监视出口并扫描人群。中国声称台湾是自己的领土，尽管从未统治过台湾。
在台北一家俱乐部的聚光灯下，黄一豪向球迷和便衣警察观众提出了一个简单的问题，在他因嘲笑中国领导人而受到威胁后，黄一豪是最后一批确保当晚在笑声中结束的人。
“怎么我被车撞了，而黄仁勋却得到了漂亮的女间谍？”这位喜剧演员问道，指的是芯片制造商英伟达创始人与一名疑似中国间谍的所谓风流韵事。
然后他抛出了一句妙语：“因为习主席不希望其他女人靠近我。”
取笑自己和中国国家主席习近平是黄的喜剧例行公事的一部分，与本周重新担任首席执行官一职的英伟达大亨无关。
但在台湾检方揭露了五人用车“打断他的胳膊和腿”以惩罚他对习近平开玩笑的阴谋后，他的表演发生了严重转变。
检方警告称，如果不重罚就释放这五人，就等于“让中共将暴力黑手直接伸向台湾街头”。
文件显示，这五人被起诉的罪名包括刑事恐吓和企图袭击等。
据称，一名中国公民向一名台湾男子支付了 25 万新台币（9,800 新元）以确保他无法演出，9 月份黄被车撞，受了轻伤。
台湾陆委会主任邱垂正表示：“我们不认为这仅仅是黄一浩的个人问题。” “这是对我们捍卫言论自由和自由民主生活方式的挑战。”
中国台湾事务办公室十月驳回了台湾参与此次袭击的指控。
台湾执政党民进党政府在本周末地方选举前捏造指控抹黑中国、煽动反华情绪并谋取政治利益。
“每年都会表演同样的戏法，观众早已厌倦了，”新闻发言人陈滨华告诉记者。
黄先生站在台北的前线，拒绝承认中国的主权主张，并称其为北京的“跨国镇压”。
这场行动的范围从恐吓和暴力到信息战，甚至与有组织犯罪勾结，针对中国视为“分裂分子”或政治嫌疑的台湾人。
过去三年，已有131人成为此类中国人的受害者

Taiwan comic takes a hit – and keeps the Xi jokes coming | The Straits Times
Taiwan comic takes a hit – and keeps the Xi Jinping jokes coming
Sign up now: Get insights on Asia's fast-moving developments
Taiwanese comic Huang Yi-Hao performs at Two Three Comedy Club in Taipei.
Published Nov 25, 2026, 02:00 PM
Updated Nov 25, 2026, 02:05 PM
Taiwanese comedian Huang Yi-Hao has kept using China’s leader Xi Jinping as a punchline despite threats that have required him to get a security detail.
Prosecutors said five people plotted to “break his arms and legs” with a car. The suspects were indicted after Huang was hit and slightly injured in September.
Taipei calls this “transnational repression” by China, saying it threatens free speech. Beijing denies involvement and says Taiwan is using the case for political gain.
TAIPEI – Even a stand-up comedian now comes with a security detail to watch the exits and scan the crowd as he fires off jokes in democratic Taiwan, claimed by China as its own territory despite never having governed it.
In the spotlight at a Taipei club, Huang Yi-Hao put a simple question to an audience of fans and plainclothes officers, the last group there to ensure the night ended only in laughter after he drew threats for jesting about China’s leader.
“How come I’m the one who gets hit by a car while Jensen Huang gets the beautiful female spy?” the comedian asked, referring to the alleged affair the founder of chipmaker Nvidia had with a suspected Chinese spy.
Then he dropped the punch line: “Because Chairman Xi doesn’t want other women anywhere near me.”
Poking fun at himself and Chinese President Xi Jinping is part of the comedy routine for Huang, not related to the Nvidia tycoon, who returned to the CEO role this week.
But his performances took a serious turn after Taiwan prosecutors uncovered a plot by five people to “break his arms and legs” with a car to punish him for his jokes about Xi.
Letting off the five without heavy punishment would amount to “allowing the Chinese Communist Party to extend its violent black hand directly into Taiwan’s streets”, prosecutors warned.
The five were indicted on charges ranging from criminal intimidation to attempted assault, the papers showed.
Huang suffered slight injuries when he was hit by a car in September after a Chinese national allegedly paid a Taiwanese man T$250,000 (S$9,800) to make sure he was unable to perform.
“We do not see this as merely a personal matter for Huang Yi-hao,” Chiu Chui-cheng, who heads Taiwan’s Mainland Affairs Council, said. “It is a challenge to our defence of free speech and a free, democratic way of life.”
China’s Taiwan Affairs Office dismissed in October Taiwan’s accusations of involvement in the attack.
The government of Taiwan’s ruling Democratic Progressive Party was fabricating allegations to smear China, stir up anti-China sentiment and seek political gain ahead of local elections this weekend, it added.
“The same trick is performed every year, and the audience has long grown tired of it,” spokesman Chen Binhua told reporters.
Huang stands on the front lines of efforts that Taipei, which rejects China’s sovereignty claims, characterises as “transnational repression” by Beijing.
The campaign ranges from intimidation and violence to information warfare and even tie-ups with organised crime to target those in Taiwan whom China views as “separatists” or politically suspect.
Over the past three years, 131 people have fallen victim to such Chinese repression, the Mainland Affairs Council says, even though its legal system is independent of China’s.
They include journalists, artists and politicians such as Puma Shen, who is running for Taipei mayor in the face of a Chinese police investigation for “separatism”.
“Mainland China uses such trans-border repression to keep asserting jurisdiction over Taiwan, in an effort to achieve the so-called political effect of ‘governing before unification’,” Chiu said.
He was referring to Beijing’s goal of bringing Taiwan under its control, by force, if necessary.
Chiu said past Chinese tactics ranged from physical attacks and surveillance to business sanctions, criminal prosecutions and digital harassment, including doxxing, or online exposure of personal details, from addresses to family ties.
Taiwan protects freedom of speech, but China tolerates no criticism of government leaders.
Huang said he was targeted for his use of “guankou”, a rapid-fire technique of traditional Chinese comedy, to criticise Xi’s rule, in a performance that went viral online in 2025.
The familiar format made the video recognisable to Chinese audiences, who could then relate to it, he said.
Yet, the attack has already achieved some of its purpose in dividing society, Huang said. Some responded to the incident by calling for a stronger defence of freedom, but others urged people to keep their heads down and avoid politics.
“Some would say: ‘Don’t talk politics, and they won’t bother you’,” Huang said, while adding that others claimed he staged the attack himself.
Had the plot succeeded, the comedian said, he would probably have gone onstage in a cast, turning even that into material about China’s activities.
“In this world, what matters most isn’t how long you live, but whether you’ve burned brightly,” he said. REUTERS

Fundraiser by Yangkey Gangshar : Nepal- Tibet Floods: Help a Mountain Guide's Wife & Children
This fund brings food, housing, and school costs to Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and children
Yangkey Gangshar is organizing this fundraiser.
Our family is heartbroken by the devastating floods that swept through communities along the Nepal–Tibet border, destroying homes, livelihoods, and taking many precious lives—including our beloved first cousin, Cho Cho Dawa Dakpu Lama Tamang.
We are Yangkey, Choenyi, Tsering, and members of the Gangshar family whose roots are deeply connected to the communities affected by this tragedy. We are raising these funds for our first cousin, Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and their two young children, who are now facing an unimaginable loss and an uncertain future.
“Cho Cho” is an endearing Tibetan term for an older brother. To our family, Cho Cho Dawa was a beloved husband, father, son, brother, nephew, cousin, and friend.
A Father Who Gave Everything for His Family
At 45 years old, Cho Cho Dawa worked as a mountain guide in Nepal’s Langtang region, providing for his wife and two children. His work often took him away from home for weeks or months at a time, but he took great pride in what he did. He was known for his warmth, kindness, generosity, and joyful spirit.
Tragically, the mountains he knew so well and worked in to support his family became the place where he lost his life.
He leaves behind his wife and two young children—a daughter, 11, and a son, 7. They are now facing not only the devastating loss of their husband and father, but the uncertainty of rebuilding their lives without the person who provided for their family.
The picture attached captures Cho Cho Dawa with his family dressed in our traditional Tibetan attire while celebrating Losar, the Tibetan New Year.
Our Family’s Connection to This Community
Our connection to this region goes back generations.
Our father and his family originally came from Kyidong (Kyirong, སྐྱིད་གྲོང་) in Tibet, a place now often referred to as Gyirong in international news. In 1959, our grandparents and relatives were forced to flee Tibet and eventually found refuge and a new home in the border regions of Nepal.
Our father and his siblings grew up in the Syabru besi and Briddhim communities, where they went to school, formed lifelong friendships, and began rebuilding their lives after leaving Tibet. These communities became an important part of our family’s history and home in Nepal.
The school where our father and his siblings once studied was among the places devastated by the floods.
Yangkey was fortunate to visit Syabru besi and Briddhim in March 2014 and again with Choenyi in November 2025. During those visits, she spent time with Cho Cho Dawa, his wife, mother, and brother and was warmly welcomed into their home. The pictures included here were taken during those visits and are now incredibly meaningful to our family.
The pictures also show places we saw and experienced during our November 2025 visit. One shows a hydropower facility along the road to Syabru besi which has been damanged and another shows the homes, guesthouses, and local businesses in Syabru besi, many of which have since been washed away.
Our family was once forced to leave our homeland in Tibet and found a place in Nepal where generations of our family could rebuild their lives. Now, that same community has been devastated by another unimaginable tragedy.
What took generations to build was swept away in moments. But the lives, memories, and stories connected to these places remain.
Cho Cho Dawa is not the only loss our family is mourning.
His brother, Cho Cho Tsering, is also facing unimaginable grief, as members of his wife’s family were among those tragically swept away.
We are also mourning the many precious lives lost in this devastating tragedy, including relatives, friends, and members of the Tibetan community.
Behind every life lost is a family now facing a future without someone they love.
We are raising funds to directly support Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and two children as they begin rebuilding their lives without him.
The funds will be used specifically for:
Shelter, rent, and household expenses
School-related expenses and future education costs for the children
Medical and other essential family needs that may arise
Long-term support to help the family regain stability and rebuild their lives
100% of the funds raised through this GoFundMe will go directly toward supporting Cho Cho Dawa’s family and, if we are fortunate enough to raise more than is needed for Cho Cho Dawa’s immediate family, additional funds will be used to help other affected families in the Tibetan community of Syabru besi who have lost loved ones, homes, or their livelihoods as a result of this disaster.
Yangkey will be traveling to Nepal in approximately two weeks and plans to personally deliver the funds raised directly to the affected families. The funds will be used solely for the relief, essential needs, and family-support purposes described above.
We want to make sure the support reaches those who need it most and provides meaningful help during this incredibly difficult time.
Every donation, no matter the amount, can make a meaningful difference.
If you are unable to donate, please consider sharing this fundraiser with your friends, family, coworkers, and community. A share may help this story reach someone who is able to help.
Thank you for taking the time to hear Cho Cho Dawa’s story and for standing with his wife and children, our family, and the communities affected by this devastating tragedy.
From our family to yours, thank you for your kindness, compassion, love, and support.
Yangkey, Choenyi, Tsering & Gangshar Family

最近的乐天证券泄露事件中也泄露了客户资产数据
乐天证券周二还报告称，近 170 万个账户的客户资产信息已被泄露。 |路透社
X Facebook LinkedIn Reddit Bluesky Threads 电子邮件 打印 书签故事 复制链接
本月早些时候遭遇大规模数据泄露的乐天证券透露，泄露的信息包括约168万个客户账户的资产余额数据。
该公司周二还表示，约 14,000 套客户自我报告的年收入和约 271 万条自我报告的资产条目遭到泄露。这些仅由客户从调查问卷的选项列表中选择的数字组成；它没有包含具体的金额。
该公司表示，到目前为止，尚未发现与该事件相关的未经授权访问客户账户或欺诈交易的证据。
据称，约441万组个人信息被泄露，包括分行和客户代码、登录ID、姓名、出生日期、地址和电话号码。该公司最初于 11 月 17 日报告称，多达 447 万个数据集受到此次泄露的影响。
其中，大约 322 万个数据集属于账户持有人，约 119 万个数据集属于已提供信息但尚未开设账户的个人。
除了初次报告中披露的项目外，该公司周二还确认了受此次泄露影响的其他七类信息：性别；国籍;传真号码；公司账户信息；开户、申请处理和取消状态；账户申请调查问卷答复；和帐户注册状态。
该公司还确定，大约 1198 万个账户的登录凭据和分支代码在此次泄露期间被泄露。
没有发现任何证据表明登录乐天证券或进行交易所需的密码、PIN 或其他信息遭到泄露。
截至周一，已有超过 60,000 人表示有兴趣对乐天证券提起集体诉讼。
负责组织潜在法律诉讼的东京牧野律师事务所表示，这次违规行为比其他事件更为严重，因为它可以向不良行为者提供一份人员名单及其资产和地址，还可以用来促进诈骗。

Data on clients’ assets also leaked in recent Rakuten Securities breach - The Japan Times
Data on clients’ assets also leaked in recent Rakuten Securities breach
Rakuten Securities additionally reported on Tuesday that information on customers' assets deposited with the company have been compromised for nearly 1.7 million accounts. | REUTERS
X Facebook LinkedIn Reddit Bluesky Threads Email Print Bookmark story Copy link
Rakuten Securities, which was hit by a massive data breach earlier this month, has disclosed that the leaked information included the asset balance data of approximately 1.68 million client accounts.
The firm also said Tuesday some 14,000 sets of clients’ self-reported annual income and roughly 2.71 million entries of self-reported assets were compromised. These consisted solely of figures selected by clients from a list of options in questionnaires; it did not contain specific monetary amounts.
The company said it has so far found no evidence of unauthorized access to client accounts or fraudulent transactions related to the incident.
It said that about 4.41 million sets of personal information, including branch and customer codes, login IDs, names, dates of birth, addresses and telephone numbers, had been leaked. The firm initially reported on Nov. 17 that up to 4.47 million data sets were affected by the breach.
Of these, roughly 3.22 million data sets belong to account holders while some 1.19 million were of individuals who have given their information but have not opened accounts.
In addition to the items disclosed in its initial report, the company on Tuesday confirmed seven other categories of information affected by the breach: gender; nationality; fax numbers; information on accounts held with the company; account openings, application processing and cancellation statuses; account application questionnaire responses; and account registration statuses.
The company has also determined that login credentials and branch codes for approximately 11.98 million accounts were leaked during the breach.
It has found no evidence of compromised passwords, PINs or other information required to log in to Rakuten Securities or conduct transactions.
More than 60,000 people had registered their interest in pursuing a class-action lawsuit against Rakuten Securities as of Monday.
Makino Law Office in Tokyo, the firm that is organizing the potential legal action, said that the breach is more serious than other incidents, as it can provide bad actors with a list of people along with their assets and addresses, and can also be used to facilitate scams.

summary: Fundraiser by Uyghur Anthology : Support the Contemporary Uyghur Anthology This anthology funds Uyghur writers and artists, translation, events, and community growth Uyghur Anthology is organizing this fundraiser. The Contemporary Uyghur An
content:
Fundraiser by Uyghur Anthology : Support the Contemporary Uyghur Anthology
This anthology funds Uyghur writers and artists, translation, events, and community growth
Uyghur Anthology is organizing this fundraiser.
The Contemporary Uyghur Anthology is a publication that platforms Uyghur (and anyone drawing their roots from East Turkistan) artists and writers in the diaspora by providing a space that is often inaccessible to those in our community. There are no other projects of its kind in the English language, and with two volumes already published, we hope to take this project to the next level. It's a rare look at Uyghur expression in an environment where all our stories are told by people pushing their own narratives without the intimate knowledge of our lived experiences.
<"Manifesto" by Sumayah Jurad from Vol. II>
We asked ourselves these questions - why wait for others to invite us to the table when we can pull up a chair and introduce ourselves? Why let others speak for us without trying first to speak? Our broken English can only be improved with audacity, and world literature is only enriched by the presence of new voices.
All-in-all, our efforts have been met with support from our community and pleasant surprise from those who did not know what they did not know.
Somewhat unprecedented is that we publish the authors' original language alongside the translation. Our book is filled with Uyghur, Latin, Cyrillic, and Chinese script to encapsulate as much of our community's experience as we can.
There are many publications in diaspora communities that platform East and South Asians, SEA, MENA, and more. Central Asia is often underrepresented in world literature or Asia-specific publications, and occupied territories even less so. Uyghurs themselves have been a relatively new diaspora community in English-speaking countries, and haven't had the opportunities to grow their literary or artistic communities. Many don't have the tools to nurture their talents, or knowledge of creative networks or opportunities, even when many journals seek work from underrepresented groups. In instances where they are aware, it's difficult to be published in this competitive field without the education and styles that publications look for. There are only a handful of literary translators translating from Uyghur to English, and not many Uyghurs who have had the chances to develop their creative language when learning English.
To sum up, the issues were:
No spaces for Uyghur writers and artists to develop their skills
A disconnect from artist communities, be it local or online
No bridge between our native tongue and English, and in turn, world literature
So, we put together a small group at the Tarim Network to take on this challenge. Completely volunteer-run; the very essence of a passion project. We did a call-out for anything and all. New writers, established writers, any language, any genre, whatever we could print in a book. And here we were, the first book of its kind, created to speak for ourselves without outsider voices, without a publishing house, raw and straight from the source.
<From the launch of Vol. I at Harvard University>
"The Contemporary Uyghur Anthology is a collection of Uyghur reflections in diaspora. Weaving together memories of the homeland, experiences of displacement, and transitions of identities, this anthology is a creative reflection of the beauty and complexities of the Uyghur experience.
By centering Uyghur voices at the forefront, this anthology serves as a form of living memory in a pivotal moment of Uyghur history. The title Under the Mulberry Tree refers to a story from the Uyghur literary classic Ana Yurt, where youthful Nuri faces terrible injustices, separation, and turmoil; but for one moment in the Charbagh, his love for Sebihe and his own family is full, ripe, and sweet, like the mulberries from the ancient tree. In a similar way that the mulberry tree offered comforts in Nuri’s time of need, we hope this volume offers a place of reflection and celebration of Uyghur culture."
We'd partnered with a member from a Jewish organisation to run writing workshops and explain editorial processes, as we had never worked on something like this before. After that collaboration, we decided to publish a revised edition on our own. This time, we added editors' notes to the pages to explain certain terms and historical and cultural contexts - mainly for our own youth, who don't always have access to cultural education. We translated more pieces from Uyghur and Chinese. Our contributors spanned 13 countries, at all levels of experience.
Was this work sustainable? Equipped with the tools, experience, and outpouring of support from our first volume, we spent the next two years saying yes. Our first book was now in libraries, there were articles and academic papers that mentioned it, and most of all, we reaffirmed the need for this sort of work. Not only were we accepting submissions, we worked one-on-one with emerging writers and artists to edit their pieces. We also helped first-time translators have their first publications with help from more experienced translators, as well as connecting them with the original authors.
Our second volume was even better than the last. From the blurb:
"How do we respond to the unexpected, and how does it influence perceptions of ourselves or the environments in which we exist? As a diaspora population, unexpected encounters can shape and transform what it means to be Uyghur as we build a new life outside of the homeland. Encounters Under the Mulberry Tree takes on the literal, abstract, and expanded renditions of these moments. We feature contemporary and historical works, including art, poetry, and prose in five languages with contributors based in a dozen countries, from established writers like award-winning author and filmmaker Tahir Hamut Izgil, to emerging artists, writers and translators of all ages. This book is a library of vignettes that grapple with intersections and how we make sense of it all."
Five languages (Uyghur, English, Chinese, Russian, Turkish)
<Vol. II showcased at a college hosted by Rawan Mentorship>
Now we embark on our third volume. The three of us do this while maintaining full time jobs, academic careers, and other side projects. We all live in different countries and have only met in person once. But it's something that we need to do, for our community and for ourselves. Our contributors have gained so much from this experience and we want to extend this opportunity to more people. This needs to survive in order for similar initiatives to be born.
Supporting the editors - all expenses so far have been paid out-of-pocket or through book sales. We do not have any donors or sponsors (yet!).
Supporting our contributors - we cannot afford to pay any of our contributors. Despite this, we have given free copies of the book to contributors, but this is definitely leaving a dent in our pockets.
Recruiting more people - paid internships or remuneration for one-off work would help volunteers spend more time on this project in this economy.
Enhance our level of expertise - we want to improve. Workshops or courses for our editors and contributors, professional feedback, the works. Unfortunately there is no one who speaks Uyghur and who is involved in Western publishing or English literature on a professional or academic level. We would appreciate connections with professionals from any language background, or the funding to level up.
Expand our network - we'd love to promote our work at literary festivals, go to conferences, do book events, establish ourselves in the public eye, provide reader copies to reviewers, and so on. However, there is a funding barrier to overcome to be able to attend these events, organise, or pre-order books.
<Vol. I on display at the Mosquers Film Festival, 2025>
Munawwar Abdulla is an Uyghur advocate, poet, and scientist born on unceded Kaurna land (Australia) and based in Massachusetts. She co-founded The Tarim Network, runs Uyghur Collective, and collaborates on projects with Uyghur rights organisations around the world. Her writings and literary translations have been published in places such as Modern Poetry in Translation, Asymptote, the Margins, the Georgia Review, and others.
Sonya Imin is a mixed Uyghur American scholar and multi-disciplinary creative who has worked on art and film projects across the US, Europe, and Central Asia. Growing up between the borderlands of the Uyghur homeland, broader Central Asia, and the midwestern United States, interrogations of belonging, home, and displacement influence the nature of her work. Currently based in Brussels, she is working on her doctoral research on Uyghur artistic production in the diaspora.
Maidina Kadeer is a mixed Uyghur-Hui writer and editor, born in Ghulja and currently based in Montreal (Tiohtià:ke), Canada. She holds a BA in English Literature and Law and Society from Concordia University, with a focus on post- and neo-colonial literature. Her work explores Uyghur identity, history, and culture through cuisine, agriculture, and neo-colonialism. She has contributed to projects such as a poem, NinetySix, in Slavs and Tatars’ Contest of the Fruits (2021) and participates in panels and interviews on Agriculture and Food History to raise awareness about Uyghur culture.

北京—在媒体报道称华盛顿计划宣布对中国和其他国家征收新关税后，北京于11月25日敦促美国“维护贸易关系的稳定发展”。
有媒体报道称，华盛顿的新征税措施将影响中国、欧盟、日本和韩国等美国主要贸易伙伴。
当被问及华盛顿报道的计划时，中国外交部表示，关税战不符合“任何人的利益”。
外交部发言人郭家琨表示，“双方应在平等、尊重、互利的基础上协商解决有关问题”。
“所谓产能过剩是一个错误的前提。中方反对以此为政治操纵的借口，”郭在例行新闻发布会上对记者表示。
一些国家担心中国工业产能过剩 — — 据称北京生产的产品超过消费，导致市场泛滥 — — 可能会扰乱关键行业的全球供应链。
北京否认这些说法。
郭表示，中美双方应“共同努力，切实落实两国元首达成的重要共识，维护中美经贸关系稳定发展”。
中国国家主席习近平和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普于 2025 年 10 月在贸易战中达成了脆弱的休战协议，但该休战协议将于 1 月份到期。法新社

Published Nov 25, 2026, 05:02 PM
Updated Nov 25, 2026, 05:14 PM
BEIJING – Beijing urged the United States on Nov 25 to “uphold the stable development” of trade relations, after media reports said Washington was planning to announce new tariffs on China and other countries.
Reports from media outlets said that Washington’s new levies would affect major US trading partners including China, the European Union, Japan and South Korea.
China’s foreign ministry said tariff wars were not in “anyone’s interest”, when asked about Washington’s reported plans.
“The two sides should resolve relevant issues through consultation on the basis of equality, respect and mutual benefit,” foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said.
“The so-called overcapacity is a false premise. China opposes using it as a pretext for political manipulation,” Guo told reporters at a regular news briefing.
Some nations fear Chinese industrial overcapacity – the claim that Beijing produces more than it consumes, flooding markets – could disrupt global supply chains in critical industries.
Beijing rejects these claims.
Guo said China and the United States should “work together to effectively implement the important consensus reached by the two heads of state and uphold the stable development of China-US economic and trade relations”.
Chinese President Xi Jinping and US counterpart Donald Trump reached a tenuous truce in their trade war in October 2025, but this will expire in January. AFP

content:
中柬举行联合军演 |海峡时报
中柬举行联合军演
立即注册：深入了解亚洲的快速发展
第八次“金龙”演习将聚焦“联合反恐反海盗行动”。
发表于 2026 年 11 月 25 日，下午 04:06
更新于 2026 年 11 月 25 日 04:09
中国和柬埔寨于11月25日开始第八次“金龙”演习。金边表示，这是迄今为止规模最大的一次，在三个地点有近3000名人员。
演习重点是“联合反恐反海盗行动”和人道主义救援。这些演习将持续到 12 月中旬，包括陆地、海上和空中演习。
云朗海军基地的开放引起了美国对中国在那里扮演的角色的担忧。柬埔寨表示，演习不会威胁任何第三国，旨在“加强共同和平和人道主义救援”。
金边 — — 坚定的盟友中国和柬埔寨于 11 月 25 日开始联合军事演习，金边称这是迄今为止最大规模的一次联合军事演习，三个地点有近 3000 名人员参加。
中国国防部在一份声明中表示，第八次“金龙”演习将重点关注“联合反恐、反海盗行动”以及人道主义救援，并将持续到12月中旬。
开幕式在位于泰国湾柬埔寨南部海岸的云朗海军基地举行，中国对该基地的改造工程引起了美国的担忧。
华盛顿表示，该基地最初部分由美国资金建造，可以让中国在有争议的南海附近获得关键的战略地位，北京声称对南海几乎整个海域拥有主权。
柬埔寨领导人一再否认该基地可供任何单一外国势力使用，今年一月，一艘美国军舰曾停靠该基地。
柬埔寨首相洪马内8月宣布，拖延已久的与美国的联合军演将于2027年重启。
两国举行了长达七年的联合演习，但金边于 2017 年初取消了联合演习，而就在与中国举行首次金龙演习几个月后。
柬埔寨国防部长蒂西哈在11月25日的讲话中表示，与中国的演习“无意威胁或对任何第三国造成影响”。
相反，他表示演习是对国际社会“加强共同和平和人道主义救援”的贡献。
他说，这些行动涵盖了陆地、海上和空中的行动，涉及军舰、无人机、直升机、装甲车、火炮和指挥系统。
柬埔寨皇家武装部队 (RCAF) 高级军官 Pen Sokrethvithyea 表示，这次演习的规模比 2025 年的演习规模还要大，而 2025 年的演习规模被称为有史以来规模最大的一次。
他说，有超过 2,900 名人员参与其中，其中约 1,300 名中国人。
皇家空军表示，2025年有近900名中国军人和1300多名柬埔寨士兵参加。
中国国防部表示，2026年的演习旨在“加强政治互信，扩大军事交流”。法新社

China and Cambodia stage joint military drills
Sign up now: Get insights on Asia's fast-moving developments
The eighth “Golden Dragon” exercises will focus on “joint counterterrorism and anti-piracy operations”.
Published Nov 25, 2026, 04:06 PM
Updated Nov 25, 2026, 04:09 PM
China and Cambodia began their eighth "Golden Dragon" drills on Nov 25. Phnom Penh said they are the largest yet, with nearly 3,000 personnel at three sites.
The exercises focus on "joint counterterrorism and anti-piracy operations" and humanitarian relief. They run until mid-December and include land, sea and air drills.
The Ream Naval Base opening drew US concern over China’s role there. Cambodia said the drills do not threaten any third country and aim to "strengthen shared peace and humanitarian relief".
PHNOM PENH – Staunch allies China and Cambodia began joint military exercises on Nov 25, which Phnom Penh said were the largest yet, featuring nearly 3,000 personnel across three locations.
The eighth “Golden Dragon” exercises will focus on “joint counterterrorism and anti-piracy operations” as well as humanitarian relief, and run until mid-December, China’s defence ministry said in a statement.
The opening ceremony was held at Ream Naval Base, located off Cambodia’s southern coast in the Gulf of Thailand, where Chinese renovations have raised US concerns.
Washington says the base – which was originally built partly with US funds – could give China a key strategic position near the disputed South China Sea, which Beijing claims almost in its entirety.
Cambodian leaders have repeatedly denied the base is for use by any single foreign power, and in January, a US warship made a port call there.
Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet announced in August that long-delayed joint military exercises with the United States would restart in 2027.
The two nations staged joint exercises for seven years before Phnom Penh scrapped them in early 2017, just months after holding its first Golden Dragon drills with China.
In remarks on Nov 25, Cambodian Defence Minister Tea Seiha said the exercises with China have “no intention of threatening or causing impact to any third country”.
Instead, he said the drills were a contribution to the international community “to strengthen shared peace and humanitarian relief”.
He said they covered operations on land, at sea and in the air, involving warships, drones, helicopters, armoured vehicles, artillery and command systems.
Royal Cambodian Armed Forces (RCAF) senior officer Pen Sokrethvithyea said they were bigger than 2025’s drills, which had been billed as the largest ever.
More than 2,900 personnel were involved, around 1,300 of them Chinese, he said.
In 2025, the RCAF said nearly 900 Chinese military personnel and more than 1,300 Cambodian soldiers took part.
The Chinese defence ministry said 2026’s exercises were aimed at “strengthening political mutual trust and expanding military exchanges”. AFP

content:
在中国全力争取将《海洋生物多样性协定》秘书处设在厦门之际，美国支持比利时和智利合并申办《海洋生物多样性协定》秘书处。图为11月4日的厦门鼓浪屿。 （新华社）
中美在全球海洋治理领域出现新一轮交锋。在中国全力争取将《海洋生物多样性协定》秘书处设在厦门之际，美国支持比利时和智利合并申办《海洋生物多样性协定》秘书处。对此北京回应，美国对秘书处选址“没有发言权”，并呼吁各方警惕申办工作被政治化、对抗化。
中国外交部发言人郭嘉昆星期三（11月25日）在例行记者会上说，美国既不是《联合国海洋法公约》的缔约国，也不是《海洋生物多样性协定》的缔约国，对协定秘书处选址事宜没有发言权。
郭嘉昆呼吁各方警惕申办工作政治化、对抗化，并称中国作为协定首批签署国、缔约国和最大会费国，愿与国际社会一道推动秘书处选址工作朝着正确方向进行。
中国今年1月宣布提名厦门申办协定秘书处。比利时和智利本月6日宣布合并申办，拟将秘书处设在智利瓦尔帕莱索，信息交换机制设在比利时布鲁塞尔，并将布鲁塞尔作为附属机构会议举办地。
中国外交部此前称，厦门已获得协定多数缔约国支持，并指比智联合申办方案违反协定规定和公平竞争原则。中国外交部发言人毛宁11月12日称，“中国期待与各方一道，推动秘书处选址工作朝着正确方向进行，维护国际社会特别是发展中国家整体和根本利益”。
美国国务院星期二（24日）发表声明，欢迎比智联合申办，并鼓励各缔约方在明年1月举行的首届缔约方大会上支持这一方案。
《海洋生物多样性协定》是《联合国海洋法公约》框架下的重要国际协定，今年1月正式生效，旨在规范国家管辖范围以外海域的生物多样性保护和可持续利用，是全球海洋治理的重要新机制。美国已签署协定，但尚未完成批准程序。
协定首届缔约方大会将于明年1月11日至22日在纽约联合国总部举行，届时将决定秘书处选址。

台北市長蔣萬安（紅衣者）25日赴士林、北投區車掃衝刺選情，前台大校長管中閔（右）陪同拜票。中央社記者葉蓁芸攝 115年11月25日
（中央社記者葉蓁芸台北25日電）選戰進入最後階段，台北市長蔣萬安今天下午赴士林、北投車掃拜票，預計晚間持續在此區舉辦「安可場」車掃。他表示，士林、北投本就幅員廣大，也是最後衝刺的重點區域。
九合一大選倒數，蔣萬安下午赴士林、北投區車掃，國民黨北市議員張斯綱、汪志冰、林杏兒、議員候選人林揚庭、賴苡任等人到場，前台北市議長吳碧珠現身力挺，前國立台灣大學校長管中閔則將一同車掃。
媒體詢問，車掃拉長到晚間，是否考量到此區選情較膠著，且民進黨台北市長候選人沈伯洋晚間也將在此舉辦活動。蔣萬安回應，士林、北投本就幅員廣大，也會是最後衝刺的重點區域。
針對管中閔陪同車掃，蔣萬安說，管中閔一直以來給他很多建議，尤其在市政上非常具有經驗，除了管中閔，吳碧珠也根據過去累積的經驗與熟悉度，給予很多指導，所以今天特別邀請管中閔一起車掃。
媒體也詢問管中閔，對於蔣萬安近來被攻擊的想法。管中閔說，當然不贊成，他知道網路、媒體鋪天蓋地抹黑和造謠對人的傷害有多大，所以更要呼籲民眾認清事實，他在蔣萬安競總成立時提到「天道酬勤」，今天要用選票酬勤，回報蔣萬安4年來的辛苦。
媒體問及，車掃期間發生多起民眾穿越馬路的狀況，雖已宣導但效果似乎不顯著。蔣萬安說，會再請團隊加強宣導，也會再次提醒支持者注意安全。至於上午在中正、萬華區車掃時，車隊疑闖紅燈，他說，會請團隊注意行車安全，遵守相關規定。
沈伯洋接受「時代雜誌」專訪，提出以社區連結打造城市韌性的願景，解決現代人的孤獨感並重建社區關係，能有效強化城市韌性。
蔣萬安表示，台北的步調很快，大家都努力打拚，有時跑行程到深夜、回到家時也能體會到孤獨感，尤其北漂青年或獨居長輩。台北的另一面也是尊重與包容，有很大的自由空間，市府近年透過改造各種公共空間、社區交流及照顧，讓大家獨處時能有安全感，在需要人群的時候有照顧感。
另外，國民黨北市議員秦慧珠今天在臉書發文指出，她的信義競選服務處遭1名男子2度到場鬧事，已報警處理。蔣萬安對此回應，再次呼籲所有民眾，選舉最後3天一定要保持理性，不要過於激動，可以有熱情，但一切言行必須要理性，好好溝通、說明。（編輯：蕭博文）1151125

发表于 2026 年 11 月 25 日 02:11

香港 — — 保护组织称，由于野生动物贸易规模超出监管范围，每小时约有 80 只活体外来动物被进口到香港，并警告病原体和寄生虫可能威胁人类和本土野生动物的健康。
ADM 资本基金会 (ADMCF) 本周发布的研究显示，2020 年至 2025 年间，该市从 86 个国家和司法管辖区进口了 370 万只活体外来动物，将自己定位为全球最大的濒危爬行动物进口国。
11 月 24 日，在香港立法会，包括 ADMCF、世界自然基金会香港分会、嘉道理农场及植物园 (KFBG)、防止虐待动物协会和当地立法者在内的团体呼吁制定一份批准进口、销售和作为宠物饲养的物种的“肯定清单”。
立法委员伊丽莎白·夸特表示，政府应及时审查和更新这样的清单，同时重新审视“动物”的法律定义，根据现有的贸易法规，“动物”不包括两栖动物和无脊椎动物。
香港渔农自然护理署没有立即回应置评请求。
新加坡等区域邻国已经实施了肯定列表模式，新加坡禁止饲养最外来的野生动物，而韩国最近颁布了立法来规范外来宠物咖啡馆和私人所有权。
KFBG 的保护经理杨建环表示，其野生动物救援中心发现饲养外来爬行动物的趋势日益明显，其中包括毒蛇物种。
杨还指出，壶菌（导致全球两栖动物急剧减少）很可能是通过释放外来两栖动物而引入香港的。
此前，香港一家爬行动物教育中心的业主曾共同主办了一次大型儿童野生动物博览会，该中心的业主在八月份被指控非法拥有濒危物种，随后发出了这一警告。路透社

Hong Kong wildlife groups push for tighter exotic pet rules after 3.7 million imports

Wild Animal Rescue Centre was seeing a growing trend in the keeping of exotic reptiles, including venomous snake species.
Published Nov 25, 2026, 02:11 PM
Updated Nov 25, 2026, 03:32 PM
HONG KONG – Every hour, some 80 live exotic animals are imported into Hong Kong as a vast wildlife trade outpaces regulation, conservation groups said, warning of pathogens and parasites that threaten the health of humans and native wildlife.
The city imported 3.7 million live exotic animals from 86 countries and jurisdictions between 2020 and 2025, positioning itself as the largest global importer of endangered reptile species, according to research released this week by the ADM Capital Foundation (ADMCF).
At Hong Kong’s Legislative Council on Nov 24, groups including ADMCF, WWF-Hong Kong, Kadoorie Farm and Botanic Garden (KFBG), the SPCA and local lawmakers called for a “Positive List” of species approved for import, sale and keeping as pets.
Legislator Elizabeth Quat said the government should review and update such a list in a timely manner, while also revisiting the legal definition of “animal”, which, under existing trade regulations, excludes amphibians and invertebrates.
Hong Kong’s Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
A Positive List model is already in place in regional neighbours such as Singapore, which bans the keeping of most exotic wildlife, and South Korea, which recently enacted legislation to regulate exotic pet cafes and private ownership.
Jianhuan Yang, conservation manager at KFBG, said its Wild Animal Rescue Centre was seeing a growing trend in the keeping of exotic reptiles, including venomous snake species.
Yang also pointed to the chytrid fungus – which has caused dramatic global amphibian declines – as likely to have been introduced into Hong Kong by the release of exotic amphibians.
The warning follows the charging in August of the owner of a Hong Kong reptile education centre, who co-hosted a major wildlife expo for children, with the illegal possession of endangered species. REUTERS

title: 沈伯洋质疑双城论坛成效 主张台北与北京办论坛
summary: 台湾“九合一”地方选举临近，民进党台北市长候选人沈伯洋称，台北与上海举办多年的双城论坛成效有限，并主张台北应考虑与北京举办城市交流论坛。图为沈伯洋11月4日在台北办公室接受路透社采访。 （路透社档案照片） 台湾“九合一”地方选举临近，民进党台北市长候选人沈伯洋称，台北与上海举办多年的双城论坛成效有限，并主张台北应考虑与北京举办城市交流论坛。 美国《时代》杂志星期三（11月25日）刊登沈伯洋专访。现年44岁的他将在星期六（28日）举行的地方选举中，挑战寻求连任的国民党籍台北市长
content:
台湾“九合一”地方选举临近，民进党台北市长候选人沈伯洋称，台北与上海举办多年的双城论坛成效有限，并主张台北应考虑与北京举办城市交流论坛。图为沈伯洋11月4日在台北办公室接受路透社采访。 （路透社档案照片）
台湾“九合一”地方选举临近，民进党台北市长候选人沈伯洋称，台北与上海举办多年的双城论坛成效有限，并主张台北应考虑与北京举办城市交流论坛。
美国《时代》杂志星期三（11月25日）刊登沈伯洋专访。现年44岁的他将在星期六（28日）举行的地方选举中，挑战寻求连任的国民党籍台北市长蒋万安。
沈伯洋说，台沪双城论坛已举办10多年，但活动往往停留在宣读文件、拍照留念，缺乏实质成效。他以台北具有“首都”地位为由，认为若要举办这类论坛，应考虑直接与北京交流。
但他强调，城市交流必须做好风险管理。他指出，北京对台湾存在武力威胁，若合作涉及交通数据等敏感资料，就须审慎评估风险。他不主张全面中断交流，而是认为交流应有实效、扩大参与，同时管控风险，并加强台北与其他国际城市的合作。
谈及大陆对台影响力行动，沈伯洋认为，台湾政府应着重预防与保护，而不是将经常往返两岸的民众一概视为可疑对象。他说，赴大陆工作的商人、歌手和演员，可能因当地商业利益受到施压，本身也可能是遭胁迫的受害者。
他说，对于可能接触大陆统战部门的民众，政府应提供必要协助，而不是在他们返台后便贴上间谍标签。他以公职人员赴大陆前的申报制度为例，指出政府可事先提醒哪些对象应避免接触，以及遭到威胁时如何应对，帮助当事人提前做好准备。
沈伯洋说，这类措施应以保护民众为出发点，而不是等到事件发生后才追究责任。在民主社会，事前做好风险管理是更好的做法。
至于两岸缺乏对话，他认为，直接沟通渠道仍然重要，并称台湾希望建立联系，但北京拒绝。在北京仍对台构成武力威胁的情况下，他主张台湾强化防空系统、发展无人机等防卫能力，以实力维护和平。
